chapters.title: Chapter 251: The VR Workers and the Real Price
paragraphs: Alfie scowled, ready to push the boy aside, but before he could move, Farrah slapped the back of his head.
"Hey!" Alfie was surprised as he rubbed the spot.
Farrah glared at him. "He must be hungry or something. Don’t you feel sorry for the kid?"
Alfie frowned but didn’t argue. He wanted to say something at first, but his hands dropped to his sides.

The boy, thin and ragged, looked up at them with wide eyes. His blue hair was messy, his cheeks hollow, and his clothes smelled faintly of sweat and dust. Yet there was a spark of determination in his gaze.
"Please," he said, voice trembling but firm. "Hire me. I can be your guide... or help you with errands. Just one C‐Grade Core for the whole day."
Kai raised an eyebrow. "Hire you?"
He didn’t expect that the boy would offer his services.
The boy nodded quickly. "Yes. My name is Xian. I know the streets, the shops, and the shortcuts. I can show you where to find things. One C‐Grade Core is enough. I won’t ask for more."
The group exchanged glances.
Alfie snorted. "One core? That’s cheap. But why us? Are you going to lead us to a shady place to capture us, then sell our organs?"
He had watched many documentaries back on Earth, and he knew something like this could happen.
Kai didn’t answer immediately.
Instead, he studied the boy carefully. Something about his desperation felt genuine, but he wasn’t about to hand over resources without knowing more.
"We’re not hiring anyone yet," Kai said evenly. "But tell me... what do you know about the Divine Gene?"
Xian’s eyes widened as he heard this... He then hesitated for a moment, then shook his head. "Not much. Only rumors. Everyone talks about it, but no one has proof. I... I don’t know if it’s real."
Mei tilted her head. "Then why do you look so desperate to work for us?"

Xian’s lips pressed together. He looked down at his worn shoes, then back up at them. "Because I want to be hired by someone... anyone... to work inside Perfect World. I... I just thought that you might be looking for one."
That caught them off guard.
Kai frowned. "Work inside Perfect World? What do you mean?"
Xian took a deep breath as he realized that these people were completely ignorant.
It was quite disappointing how clueless they were, but he decided to explain further, hoping to earn a tip.

"Yes... Organizations hire capable people to be laborers in the game. They need workers for mining, gathering resources, delivery tasks... all kinds of jobs. It’s like real work, but inside Perfect World. You earn credits, sometimes even items, and if you’re lucky, you can bring things back through the Transference Nodes."
The group exchanged glances.
Their understanding of the virtual world just kept expanding.
Claire muttered, "So Perfect World isn’t just training or entertainment... it’s an economy or something..."
Ralph rubbed his chin. "Mining, gathering, delivery... it sounds like they’re treating it like another world entirely. Well, since the Transference Node exists, I guess that made a lot of sense."
Mei’s eyes widened. "A second civilization... inside a game."
Kai listened silently...
He didn’t expect that the Perfect World was being used like that. But just like what Ralph said, it certainly started making sense.
Still, he couldn’t understand why Xian wanted to work like that. "Why risk yourself in a place like that?" Kai asked.
Xian’s expression hardened.
His voice trembled as he tried to control his emotions.
"Because I want to find the Divine Gene. If I can get it... if I can claim the reward... I can save my sister."
The group froze.
Farrah’s eyes softened. "Your sister?"

Xian nodded... "She’s sick. A disease that no doctor here can cure. Medicines are too expensive, and the factions don’t care about people like us. But if I find the Divine Gene... if I get the treasures and medicines they promise... I can save her."
Silence fell over the group.
That seemed quite impossible to happen. If the Divine Gene were easy to find, the large organizations would’ve discovered it already.
Alfie scratched his head, suddenly uncomfortable. "Damn... that’s heavy."
Claire frowned as she really didn’t like seeing children suffer.
"So you’re willing to risk everything... just for her?"

"Yes," Xian said firmly. "Even if it means working as a laborer inside Perfect World. Even if it means mining for scraps or delivering packages. I’ll do anything. Because one day... maybe I’ll stumble across the Divine Gene. And then... she’ll live."
Mei’s chest tightened. She could see the desperation in the boy’s eyes, the determination of someone with nothing left but hope.
"He’s serious..."
Kai looked at his team. They were all thinking the same thing. Perfect World wasn’t just a distraction or entertainment... It could also be a place of hope.
Xian stood there, waiting... "Please. Just one C‐Grade Core. I’ll guide you anywhere in the city. I’ll prove I’m useful."
Kai finally smiled.
In the end, they certainly needed a guide. So he decided to give the boy a chance. "Alright, Xian. We’ll take you on as our guide."
Xian’s face lit up with relief, but Kai quickly pressed further. "Then tell me... where can we purchase a cheap Transference Box?"

The boy’s smile as he looked at the nearby shop... Then, his smile faltered for a moment as he recalled something. His eyes turned toward Kai’s pouch. "Wait... Before that, I saw you buy the storage stick for Perfect World just now. Is it with you?"
Kai blinked, confused. "What do you mean?"
Xian gave a helpless smile. "That installer... it usually costs only two C‐Grade Energy Cores."
Kai’s eyes widened in shock. The others froze, also stunned by the revelation.
Mei and Claire immediately wanted to storm back into the Immersion Hub, but Xian quickly reminded them, "You already agreed to the price. Once the cores are paid, there’s no refund."
The group exchanged frustrated looks, but in the end, he was right... They didn’t even bother checking the other store’s price!
They could only sigh and thank Xian for informing them.
Kai tightened his grip on the pouch and shook his head. He got played, but he didn’t really feel that bad.
"Alright... Show us around this city."
And just like that, the boy became their guide...

chapters.title: Chapter 252: Selling the Infinite Supply
paragraphs: Kai and the others were still curious about the Virtual World, but since they did not have any pods just yet, they all noted its existence in their minds.
Nonetheless, Xian quickly proved his worth as a guide.
He led Kai and the others through Cameron City’s crowded streets, pointing out which shops were trustworthy and which ones were notorious for scamming newcomers.
"See that stall?" he whispered, gesturing toward a vendor with flashy signs.
"They’ll charge you double. Stick to the shops near the east market... those merchants are honest."
His advice would surely save them from wasting more cores. Just like that, the group realized how valuable his knowledge was.
After a while, Xian frowned at their appearance.
"Everyone’s looking at you... You should really change your clothes," he suggested. "Right now, you look like outsiders. To vendors, that’s basically announcing you’re easy targets."

Kai didn’t think it was that bad, but after noticing the way merchants eyed them, he yielded. Soon, they purchased sets of new clothes that matched the city’s fashion sense... practical tunics, dark trousers, and light jackets that blended in with the crowd.
The transformation was immediate... they no longer stood out like lost travelers.
As they continued walking, Kai noticed Xian’s eyes drifting toward food stalls.
Soon, his stomach growled faintly, though he tried to hide it. Concerned, Kai asked him to find an inn where they could rent rooms and eat.
Anyway, they had to find a place as well.
"Of course! Follow me!"
Xian nodded eagerly and guided them to a modest establishment with a sign called Silver Rest Inn.
The inn was simple but clean, with sturdy wooden doors and a faint smell of stew wafting from the kitchen.
Just like that, they rented three rooms, two people per room, enough for the six of them.
The innkeeper served meals as part of the lodging... There were bowls of rice, stewed vegetables, and slices of salted meat.
It wasn’t luxurious, but it was warm and filling. The group ate gratefully, enjoying the comfort of a proper meal after the chaos outside the city walls.

Xian, however, didn’t touch his food. Instead, he carefully wrapped his portion in a small plastic bag, clearly intending to save it. Kai and the others exchanged knowing looks... it was obvious the food was meant for his sister.
Without saying much, Kai ordered another set of meals and placed it in front of him.
"This one’s for you. Eat."
Xian hesitated with his eyes flickering with guilt, but then his expression softened. He nodded gratefully and ate joyfully, savoring every bite as if it were the best meal he’d had in weeks.
Afterward, the group discussed their plans.
Cameron City was vast, and there was much to explore. They decided to split up to cover more ground.
Xian would continue guiding Kai, Mei, and Farrah, while Claire, Alfie, and Ralph chose to explore on their own.
And so, their first day in Cameron City truly began... With new clothes to blend in, a guide they could trust, and the technologies they had never seen before.
Kai’s team followed Xian deeper into Cameron City, leaving behind the noisy marketplace and crowded stalls.
Kai was really curious about the weapon shops within the city, but unfortunately, the decent weapons like high-caliber guns, Plasma Rifles, and others were being controlled by the Factions.
Of course, it didn’t mean that they would only sell to faction members, but it meant the location of the vendors would be deeper within the city.
Just like that, the streets gradually grew quieter, as the shouting vendors and clattering carts lessened...
Kai wasn’t sure how it was divided, but it seemed that the shops were directly owned by the 12 Factions of Cameron.
Here, the shops were more specialized... Kai could already see items from high-quality weapons to luxurious decorations...

Xian pointed them out as they walked. "This area’s different. You’ll find expert smiths who repair weapons, tailors who make custom gear, and a few apothecaries who sell medicine without mixing it with junk. The prices are fairer here, but you still need to be careful."
Mei peered into one shop where a craftsman was polishing a blade. "It feels calmer here," she murmured.
Farrah nodded. "Maybe less chaos... more business."
Kai wanted to ask more about the Factions, but for now, he wasn’t in a hurry.
They passed a row of herbal shops, filled with the scent of dried leaves and roots.
’Hmm?’ Kai was curious as he saw Xian looking at this store longingly.
"Do you want to enter and buy something in the shop? We can wait..."
"N‐no, sir!" Xian stammered, quickly waving his hand.
Kai just chuckled and led the team inside anyway. He hadn’t chosen this shop at random... entering here had been one of his aims all along.
As Kai and his team stepped into the herbal shop, they immediately felt overwhelmed with the scent of medicine.
Kai smiled at this, and soon, he looked behind the counter where an old shopkeeper was seated.
She greeted them with a nod, then gestured toward the shelves lined with tonics and vials.
Kai and the others moved closer, scanning the neatly displayed bottles. Each had a handwritten tag with its name and price...
[ Vitality Tonic - 3 C‐Grade Cores ]
[ Ironbody Extract - 4 C‐Grade Cores ]
[ Spirit Recovery Serum - 5 C‐Grade Cores ]
[ Blood Accelerator - 6 C‐Grade Cores ]
The prices gave Kai a clear idea of the market value. These tonics promised effects ranging from stamina recovery to enhanced reflexes, though none seemed extraordinary.
Kai reached into his pouch and pulled out a slim, metallic injector with a faintly blue vial chamber...
Needless to say, it was the Gene Stimulant Injector from his Water Gift Pack. He held it up casually and showed it with confidence.
"Are you buying something like this?"
The old shopkeeper wanted to ignore him at first, but soon her eyes widened as she recognized it!
She leaned forward, her hands trembling slightly. "Yes... yes! I’ll pay five C‐Grade Crystals for this!"
Kai glanced at the displayed tonics again. The price matched what she offered... reasonable, considering the stimulant’s effects were likely stronger than the tonics on her shelves.
He smiled faintly. "Make it seven, and I’ll sell all of my Gene Stimulants only to you."

chapters.title: Chapter 253: Earning Money and Avoiding Trouble
paragraphs: Kai’s Gene Stimulant was certainly a precious item, but it was not at a level where he could put a very high price on it yet.
[ Gene Stimulant Injector (Unique): A specialized injector containing a biochemical stimulant. Temporarily enhances cellular recovery, stamina, and reflex response.
Effects last for at least 10 minutes. ]
[ Note: Overuse may cause strain on the body. ]
The effects could only last for 10 minutes, and using them continuously would cause strain to the body.
Still, even if the shopkeeper just briefly analyzed it, she could tell that it would be a hot item once it became available to the market.
As she further looked at it, she froze, her eyes turned between Kai and the injector. She realized this was no ordinary bargain... it was a real deal.
She could probably sell it for about 10 or more C-Grade Cores as long as she knew how to handle the hype about it.
After a few tense moments, she nodded eagerly. "Agreed!"
Kai’s smile widened.
Without hesitation, he reached into his pouch and carefully laid out twenty-four more injectors on the counter. At this point, everything was sparkling in the shopkeeper’s eyes.
These things were all treasures! her expression shifting from disbelief to sheer joy.
Just like that, Kai turned the extra Gene Stimulant Injectors that he had into 175 C-Grade Crystal Cores!
Furthermore, he didn’t have to worry about where to dispose of them, since he secured a loyal contact within Cameron City.
For the shopkeeper, it was the deal of a lifetime, one that could elevate her humble herbal shop into a supplier of rare, coveted stimulants.
Mei and Farrah exchanged glances... After all, he still had another!
This next item was from the same gift pack!
"I have twenty-five of these items as well."
[ Spirit‐Boosting Potion Flask (Unique): A prepared tonic designed to restore mental clarity, focus, and Spirit Energy. Provides temporary resistance against fatigue and mental debuff. ]
[ Note: The effect weakens if consumed repeatedly in a brief period. ]
Once again, the old shopkeeper was shocked... Still, this time, she didn’t dare to miss the opportunity.
She didn’t hesitate and immediately offered 8 C-Grade Cores for each of them.

Based on her own appraisal, the potion provides about 30 to 40 Spirit Points. With that in consideration, she believed that 8 C-Grade Cores should be fair since the ones that only give about 20 Spirit Points were being sold for 5 Cores.
With Kai’s potion, he believed that he could sell it for 11 or more and profit well from it.
And just like that, Kai had made his first major transaction in Cameron City.
Xian was left speechless as they stepped out of the herbal shop. His eyes were still wide, his mind racing after watching Kai casually trade away dozens of rare stimulants and potions.
To him, it looked like something only a master alchemist could do.

"You... you’re incredible," Xian finally managed, his voice was still trembling with excitement. "I didn’t expect you’d have items like that. I thought only faction alchemists could make things like those."
Kai didn’t respond, simply walking ahead with the same calm expression. He had no intention of correcting the boy...
Nonetheless, Xian’s heart was pounding.
Hope surged through him, stronger than ever.
’If he has stimulants and potions like that... maybe he has something that could cure her...’
Gathering his courage, Xian hurried to Kai’s side. "Sir Kai," he said quietly, almost pleading, "do you... do you have a cure? For sicknesses? For someone who’s... really ill?"
Mei and Farrah exchanged glances, realizing what he meant. The boy wasn’t asking for himself... he was thinking of his sister.
Kai slowed his steps, studying Xian’s desperate expression. He didn’t answer right away...

First of all, he didn’t know how sick Xian’s sister was. He also had Medical Gift Packs, but they were mostly equipment that had to be used by medical practitioners instead of a magical medicine that could cure any disease.
"Mhm... I don’t know. We can visit her later. For now, we need to look around this city." Kai replied.
"Yes! I’ll guide you!" Xian’s eyes lit up.
He didn’t mind if Kai had the cure or not. The fact that he was willing to check his sister’s condition was already good enough for him.
Just like that, they continued looking around and passed through various stores like a cobbler shop, a bookstore, a pharmacy, a millinery or hat maker, a smithy, and others...
Soon, the street widened, and at the end stood a mansion...
"Hmm? Is this the City Mayor’s mansion or something?" Kai mused.

He looked at its tall iron gates, guarded by armored men who watched the road with sharp eyes. The building itself was imposing, with banners hanging from its walls... Well, it was a crab symbol etched in black and silver.
Kai immediately had an idea and Xian confirmed it.
"Don’t go near that place," he warned...
"That mansion belongs to one of the Twelve Factions... the Cancer Faction."
"Cancer Faction..." Kai repeated. He guessed as much.
Hale Libra, Cornelio Aries... and now, the Cancer Faction. It was indeed the Zodiac.
Xian nodded quickly.

"They’re one of the strongest groups in Cameron City. I don’t really like them compared to others. They’re more ruthless and very protective of their territory. Outsiders who wander too close might get treated as spies. You don’t want their attention."
Mei’s eyes narrowed as she studied the banners. "So each faction has its own district?"

"Exactly," Xian said. "The Aries Faction, Taurus, Cancer... all twelve have their own strongholds scattered across the city. This mansion is Cancer’s base. If you value your safety, keep your distance."
Kai glanced at the guards again.
They were humans and not Sentinels...
Their armor was polished, and their eyes were already locked onto their group...
Kai understood immediately... this wasn’t a place for casual curiosity.
"Alright," Kai said firmly. "We’ll steer clear."
Xian exhaled in relief. "Good. I don’t want you getting into trouble. The factions are powerful, and they don’t forgive mistakes."
The group turned away from the mansion to continue down the quieter streets. Kai was even planning to check the smithy just now.
However, as soon as they turned their backs, they heard the iron gates creaking open...

"Miss! Stop right there!"

sentences.text: Kai’s Gene Stimulant was certainly a precious item, but it was not at a level where he could put a very high price on it yet.
[ Gene Stimulant Injector (Unique): A specialized injector containing a biochemical stimulant.
Temporarily enhances cellular recovery, stamina, and reflex response.
Effects last for at least 10 minutes. ]
[ Note: Overuse may cause strain on the body. ]
The effects could only last for 10 minutes, and using them continuously would cause strain to the body.
Still, even if the shopkeeper just briefly analyzed it, she could tell that it would be a hot item once it became available to the market.
As she further looked at it, she froze, her eyes turned between Kai and the injector.
She realized this was no ordinary bargain... it was a real deal.
She could probably sell it for about 10 or more C-Grade Cores as long as she knew how to handle the hype about it.
After a few tense moments, she nodded eagerly.
"Agreed!"
Kai’s smile widened.
Without hesitation, he reached into his pouch and carefully laid out twenty-four more injectors on the counter.
At this point, everything was sparkling in the shopkeeper’s eyes.
These things were all treasures! her expression shifting from disbelief to sheer joy.
Just like that, Kai turned the extra Gene Stimulant Injectors that he had into 175 C-Grade Crystal Cores!
Furthermore, he didn’t have to worry about where to dispose of them, since he secured a loyal contact within Cameron City.
For the shopkeeper, it was the deal of a lifetime, one that could elevate her humble herbal shop into a supplier of rare, coveted stimulants.
Mei and Farrah exchanged glances...
After all, he still had another!
This next item was from the same gift pack!
"I have twenty-five of these items as well."
[ Spirit‐Boosting Potion Flask (Unique): A prepared tonic designed to restore mental clarity, focus, and Spirit Energy.
Provides temporary resistance against fatigue and mental debuff. ]
[ Note: The effect weakens if consumed repeatedly in a brief period. ]
Once again, the old shopkeeper was shocked...
Still, this time, she didn’t dare to miss the opportunity.
She didn’t hesitate and immediately offered 8 C-Grade Cores for each of them.
Based on her own appraisal, the potion provides about 30 to 40 Spirit Points.
With that in consideration, she believed that 8 C-Grade Cores should be fair since the ones that only give about 20 Spirit Points were being sold for 5 Cores.
With Kai’s potion, he believed that he could sell it for 11 or more and profit well from it.
And just like that, Kai had made his first major transaction in Cameron City.
Xian was left speechless as they stepped out of the herbal shop.
His eyes were still wide, his mind racing after watching Kai casually trade away dozens of rare stimulants and potions.
To him, it looked like something only a master alchemist could do.
"You... you’re incredible," Xian finally managed, his voice was still trembling with excitement.
"I didn’t expect you’d have items like that.
I thought only faction alchemists could make things like those."
Kai didn’t respond, simply walking ahead with the same calm expression.
He had no intention of correcting the boy...
Nonetheless, Xian’s heart was pounding.
Hope surged through him, stronger than ever.
’If he has stimulants and potions like that... maybe he has something that could cure her...’
Gathering his courage, Xian hurried to Kai’s side.
"Sir Kai," he said quietly, almost pleading, "do you... do you have a cure?
For sicknesses?
For someone who’s... really ill?"
Mei and Farrah exchanged glances, realizing what he meant.
The boy wasn’t asking for himself... he was thinking of his sister.
Kai slowed his steps, studying Xian’s desperate expression.
He didn’t answer right away...
First of all, he didn’t know how sick Xian’s sister was.
He also had Medical Gift Packs, but they were mostly equipment that had to be used by medical practitioners instead of a magical medicine that could cure any disease.
"Mhm...
I don’t know.
We can visit her later.
For now, we need to look around this city." Kai replied.
"Yes!
I’ll guide you!" Xian’s eyes lit up.
He didn’t mind if Kai had the cure or not.
The fact that he was willing to check his sister’s condition was already good enough for him.
Just like that, they continued looking around and passed through various stores like a cobbler shop, a bookstore, a pharmacy, a millinery or hat maker, a smithy, and others...
Soon, the street widened, and at the end stood a mansion...
"Hmm?
Is this the City Mayor’s mansion or something?" Kai mused.
He looked at its tall iron gates, guarded by armored men who watched the road with sharp eyes.
The building itself was imposing, with banners hanging from its walls...
Well, it was a crab symbol etched in black and silver.
Kai immediately had an idea and Xian confirmed it.
"Don’t go near that place," he warned...
"That mansion belongs to one of the Twelve Factions... the Cancer Faction."
"Cancer Faction..." Kai repeated.
He guessed as much.
Hale Libra, Cornelio Aries... and now, the Cancer Faction.
It was indeed the Zodiac.
Xian nodded quickly.
"They’re one of the strongest groups in Cameron City.
I don’t really like them compared to others.
They’re more ruthless and very protective of their territory.
Outsiders who wander too close might get treated as spies.
You don’t want their attention."
Mei’s eyes narrowed as she studied the banners.
"So each faction has its own district?"
"Exactly," Xian said.
"The Aries Faction, Taurus, Cancer... all twelve have their own strongholds scattered across the city.
This mansion is Cancer’s base.
If you value your safety, keep your distance."
Kai glanced at the guards again.
They were humans and not Sentinels...
Their armor was polished, and their eyes were already locked onto their group...
Kai understood immediately... this wasn’t a place for casual curiosity.
"Alright," Kai said firmly.
"We’ll steer clear."
Xian exhaled in relief.
"Good.
I don’t want you getting into trouble.
The factions are powerful, and they don’t forgive mistakes."
The group turned away from the mansion to continue down the quieter streets.
Kai was even planning to check the smithy just now.
However, as soon as they turned their backs, they heard the iron gates creaking open...
Soon, they heard a voice calling out for them...
"Miss!
Stop right there!"

chapters.title: Chapter 254: The Faction and the Threat
paragraphs: Humphrey of the Cancer Faction was a prominent figure, even among the Twelve Families. He was one of the Elders who was known to have destroyed two bases of Aria’s Rebel Army.
His face carried the sharp lines of nobility. He was already reaching the age of 50, but his appearance remained that of a man in his twenties.
He had a strong jaw, a narrow chin, and blue eyes that seemed to look a little lazy.
His blonde hair was kept neatly combed back, a deliberate style that emphasized the unusual feature hidden beneath his brow...
Well, on his forehead lay the mark of his lineage... a third eye, the product of the Cancer Faction’s unique gene mutation.
It was not always visible. Normally, it was concealed beneath a scarf or visor when he walked the streets.
The eye was rarely revealed outside of combat, for it was both a weapon and a symbol of his family’s power.
Those who had seen it in battle knew that it could pierce illusions, sense hostile intent, and even overwhelm weaker minds.
"Ahhh... I’ll enter the Perfect World later for 9 hours. Let’s finish that matter with old man Francis." Humphrey muttered as he recalled his task for today.
His daily life reflected the privilege of his station. He rose early, attended to faction duties, and oversaw the training of younger initiates.
His mornings were often spent reviewing reports from the faction’s merchants and smiths, ensuring that their trade remained profitable and their weapons were superior.
Afternoons were reserved for sparring and honing his combat skills, though he rarely revealed the full extent of his mutation as he would instead enter the VR World.

Despite the rigid structure of his life, Humphrey liked this a lot since he no longer had to go to the frontlines to fight against the A.I. Army, especially the Ascendant Units and other powerful machines that were controlled by Anima...
Still, he was ambitious, eager to prove himself worthy of the Cancer name, and constantly sought opportunities to expand his influence within the city walls...
One such opportunity lay in the smithy he had commissioned... a place where the finest weapons were forged under the faction’s patronage.

On this particular day, Humphrey left the mansion to visit Francis in the smithy. He had ordered a custom blade, one designed to channel his unique mutation more effectively. His steps were purposeful, his scarf drawn low to conceal the third eye, his guards trailing behind at a respectful distance.
But as he approached the gates, something caught his attention.
There, just beyond the iron bars, stood a small group of outsiders.
Among them was a woman whose beauty struck him like a sudden blow.
He could not mistake it!
He was a Level 50 Survivor, and this much distance was nothing to him!
He could clearly see that it wasn’t just made up! It was her bare face!
Considering how she didn’t seem to be part of the 12 Zodiacs, it must not be a face reconstruction as well.
"This... She’s mine!"
Her presence was unassuming, yet her gaze lingered on the mansion with curiosity. Humphrey froze mid‐stride, his breath catching.
For a moment, the smithy and his commission were forgotten.
He watched as the group began to turn away, clearly intending to leave.
He didn’t expect this but panic surged through him... the thought of letting her walk away without a word was unbearable.
His instincts urged him to act.
"Miss! Stop right there!" Humphrey’s voice rang out.
At the same time, the iron gates creaked open, pushed wide by the guards.
The sound echoed across the quiet street, drawing the attention of everyone nearby.
Humphrey stepped forward, his eyes locked on the woman.
His scarf concealed the third eye, but beneath it, the mutation pulsed with awareness, sensing her presence as something more than ordinary.
Meanwhile, the air grew tense as Kai’s group halted, caught between caution and curiosity.
Soon, Humphrey’s guards stood ready as they could already guess this Elder’s antics.
"Hmm?" Kai and the others glanced at the man from the Cancer Faction’s mansion.
"You there... Miss. What is your name? Which faction have you joined? If you haven’t reached Level 30 yet, I can help you. I’ll take care of you."
His tone was filled with entitlement, completely ignoring the rest of Kai’s group as if they didn’t exist.
The guards behind him stood at attention, ready to enforce his will, but his gaze never left Mei.
Mei’s stomach turned.
The way he spoke, as if she were some fragile ornament to be claimed, filled her with disgust. Still, she tried to remain civil since this wasn’t their territory...
She slightly forced herself to answer politely. "I don’t need—"
But Humphrey cut her off...

"I am Humphrey of the Cancer Faction. One of the Twelve Zodiac Families. You should feel honored that I am speaking to you. Under my care, you’ll rise quickly. You won’t have to struggle like the rest of these... outsiders."
At this point, each word grated against her patience.
She was on the verge of letting loose some words that could wound more than any weapon.
But before she could, Kai’s hand rested firmly on her shoulder.
The simple gesture was enough to calm her. He stepped forward, calmly looking at the man who called himself Humphrey and the guards around him.
"That’s enough," Kai said evenly. "We’ll be leaving now."
The words were simple, but the weight behind them silenced the tension.
Mei glanced at Kai, her anger subsided a little thanks to that.
Farrah then shifted closer, ready to support her, while Xian looked nervously between the guards and the Elder, realizing how dangerous this encounter could become.
Humphrey’s eyes squinted... He was clearly displeased at being dismissed so casually.
For a moment, it seemed a fight was about to break out right there in the street as his hands started turning red due to his Gene Skill.
But then, more and more people began to gather.

Locals stopped to watch, whispering among themselves. The sight of an Elder from the Cancer Faction confronting outsiders was enough to draw attention, and soon the quiet street was filled with curious eyes.
Humphrey immediately paused. He could not afford a public spectacle, especially when they had just suppressed the Beast-Class units of the A.I. Army...
His third eye pulsed beneath the scarf, itching to be revealed, but he restrained himself.
He took a step back and looked at Kai coldly...
"You may leave... for now. But remember this, I’ll be back for you."
His gaze then lingered on Mei before he turned away.

chapters.title: Chapter 255: Cancer Faction and the Sister
paragraphs: Kai’s group walked away from the Cancer Faction’s gates silently...
Since they were still in the territory of the enemy, they had to tread carefully.
Humphrey’s words were arrogant, dismissive, and threatening. If they provoke the nasty man, they might not care about the public and start attacking them.
They didn’t want a fight right now... Still, none of them liked the idea of being "marked" by an Elder, especially one who had made it clear he wanted Mei.
"I remember his face..." Kai muttered. His expression remained calm as he gave a death sentence to Humphrey.
Mei smiled after seeing this. She could tell what was going on in his mind. "Yes. We’ll destroy them once we get stronger."

Everyone could tell immediately that Humphrey and his guards were far above their current level. Entry into Cameron City required Level 30, but the way those men carried themselves, the confidence in their stance, and the faint aura of their Gene Skills suggested they were Level 40 or higher. It wouldn’t even be surprising if they had already fused or combined their skills...
Facing them now would be suicide.
Furthermore, they knew each faction had its own special abilities, unique mutations or techniques that gave them dominance in the city.
Without proper information, charging head‐on into conflict would be reckless. For now, they had to lie low, gather intelligence, and build their strength.
"Haha... That’s right! We’ll get back to them..." Farrah muttered under his breath, his tone steady but filled with resolve.
"First... I need to get rich..." Kai muttered.
He already had a plan forming. The Gift Packs he possessed were his greatest advantage, a source of wealth and influence if used correctly.

With them, he could flood the market with stimulants, potions, and advanced equipment. But there was a problem... he produced too many items at once. He couldn’t sell them all quickly without drawing unwanted attention.

For example, if he opened a superior‐grade Water Gift Pack just to sell Gene Stimulants and Spirit‐Boosting Potions, he would also end up with an atmospheric water generator, a portable desalination unit, a fire extinguisher, and even stainless steel tumblers. Since his inventory couldn’t store excess items indefinitely, he would have to store them somewhere or be forced to sell those as well.
That meant his presence in the market would be noticed sooner or later.
Kai considered the situation carefully. If he wanted to avoid suspicion, he might need to open a store himself... a front to sell off the surplus items without appearing desperate or careless.
But as he observed Cameron City, it was clear that the families controlled most of the trade. Independent shops were rare, and faction oversight was everywhere.
To establish a foothold, he would need backing.
"Mhmm... Is it time to visit him?" Kai mused.
His thoughts turned to Cornelio Aries, the Level 80 Survivor from the Aries Faction.
Cornelio had already shown interest in him before, and perhaps that connection could be leveraged.
With Cornelio’s support, Kai could probably secure a legitimate channel to sell his items, shielded from faction interference. It was a dangerous gamble, but one that might pay off.
For now, however, there was something more pressing. Xian’s sister.
Kai glanced at the boy, who was walking with nervous energy... It was already getting late so his eyes were darting between the streets and his companions.
He probably wanted to go home by now.
Furthermore, the encounter with Humphrey had shaken him. It was already amazing that this kid remained stuck with them.
He wanted to see Xian’s sister, to check her condition, and perhaps... just perhaps, offer her hope.
"Let’s go," Kai said firmly. "We’ll visit your sister first."
Xian’s face lit up.
"Yes! This way!" he said eagerly, leading them through the quieter streets.
Just like that, Kai’s group followed Xian eastward, leaving behind the bustling districts of Cameron City.
The streets grew narrower, and the place started being more polluted in a literal sense. The place was filled with smoke and rot.
Soon, they reached the slum quarter... a place hidden at the city’s edge, beyond the reach of the Twelve Factions. Here, the families had little interest in control.
It was where junk was dumped, trash burned or recycled, and where clean water was a luxury no one could afford.
The people here were skinny, their clothes ragged, and their faces streaked with dirt.
Yet despite the misery, they seemed to be eager to live just like Xian...
In any case, Xian led them through winding alleys until they reached what he called home.
Kai paused as he looked at it.
"This..."
It was hardly a house. It was just a collapsed wall propped up with tarps, enough to shield against rain and wind.
Inside, the space was cramped, forcing anyone taller than a child to bend low.
Only Kai entered fully. Mei and Farrah remained outside, peering in through the gaps.
Kai’s eyes then adjusted to the dim interior.
On a makeshift bed of old cloth lay a girl with blue hair similar to Xian.
She looked fragile, yet she managed a faint smile when she saw her brother.
"No way..."
Suddenly, Kai’s gaze froze on her left arm.
The skin had darkened, spreading from the shoulder down... It was already mottled and lifeless. It was like only a skin
He wasn’t a medical expert, but looking at it, he knew that it couldn’t stay like that.
’It must be amputated...’he thought grimly.
If left unchecked, the corruption would consume her entire body.
He wasn’t sure what it was... infection, mutation, or something worse. But one thing was clear, she wouldn’t last long.
"W-what happened to her?"
Mei gasped softly from outside.
Farrah’s expression also changed as she was shocked... It must be really painful!
Even Xian’s voice trembled as he asked, "Sir Kai... can you cure her?"
Kai didn’t answer immediately. He studied the girl carefully...
They weren’t physicians, and this wasn’t a problem that could be solved with ordinary medicine. Yet as he thought of the items in his inventory, possibilities began to form.
His eyes lit up.
"We might have a chance. But let’s have a physician check her out first..." Kai muttered.
But as he was about to call for one, he suddenly recalled his Status Crystal.
He might as well check the two of them before going.

He might as well check the two of them before going.

chapters.title: Chapter 256: The Solution
paragraphs: Kai raised the Status Crystal, its glow shimmering as he focused on Xian first.
"What is this? Wait... You have a Status Crystal?"
"Yep... Just put your hand here." Kai said.
Soon, he got the result he needed.
[ Name: Xian ]
[ Title: Scrap Survivor ]
[ Level: 3 ]
[ Health: 75 / 85 ]
[ Spirit: 30 / 30 ]
[ Physique Rating: F ]
[ Active Skills: None ]
[ Passive Skills: None ]
"Huh? You have a title? Scrap Survivor?"
Kai was shocked. Even the others who were looking at the crystal. They weren’t unfamiliar with the Survivor Title... They had seen Beginner Survivor, Skilled Survivor, and even Expert Survivor.
However, it was their first time seeing a Scrap Survivor!
Without hesitation, Kai checked the Title Effect, and he was even more surprised!

[ Scrap Survivor (Title Effect): Grants experience when successfully scavenging usable materials, repairing damaged equipment, or repurposing junk into functional items. Provides high resistance against hunger and fatigue when in 50% Health Points or lower. ]
Xian scratched his head. He didn’t know that he already had a title.
"Amazing... So I’m already Level 3... But I’ve never received any Gene Enhancement Serum."
"Well... You probably worked hard scavenging for materials or finding junk you can repurpose."
Then Kai turned the crystal toward the girl.
He then helped her other hand to touch the crystal and soon, everyone saw the result.
[ Name: Xinyi ]
[ Title: None ]
[ Level: 2 ]
[ Health: 15 / 70 ]
[ Spirit: 50 / 50 ]
[ Physique Rating: F- ]
[ Active Skills: None ]
[ Passive Skills: None ]
[ Status: Severe necrosis in the left arm. Blood circulation has failed. Corruption spreading from the shoulder to the fingertips. Health regeneration suppressed until condition is resolved. ]
Kai’s eyes narrowed. Her health bar was critically low, and the necrosis in her arm explained the imbalance. Yet her Spirit was unusually high for someone so weak.
Her level was lower than Xian, but she was still 20 points higher in terms of Spirit Points.
Of course, it was also noticed by Farrah.
"Her body is failing... but her Spirit is strong. That’s rare."
Then, finally, they noticed the strange Status.
Kai frowned as the status crystal confirmed his suspicion
"...So it’s that bad," he muttered, staring at the words. "Her arm really is gone."
Mei’s face paled. She had noticed the discoloration earlier, but seeing it spelled out in the Status made her disappointed.
"It’s worse than I thought," she said quietly. "No wonder she can barely stand."
Kai glanced at Xinyi again...
"She’s holding on with Spirit alone," he said. "That’s the only reason she’s still alive."
The three of them exchanged uneasy looks.
"Don’t worry... We have some options left."
Xian’s hands trembled as he looked at the crystal. "Really?! Can you save her?"
Kai didn’t answer immediately. He studied the young girl carefully and nodded.
"We might have a chance," he muttered. "If we can stop the corruption and keep her alive long enough... she should have a second life. Still, my solution must be done if all else fails."
Xian’s face brightened with hope, while Mei and Farrah exchanged uneasy glances. They had no idea what Kai was about to do.
Kai didn’t waste time. He left the cramped room and pushed through the narrow alleys of the slums, recalling the small clinic where a physician kept his practice...
The man’s name was Chrisome... At the very least, he was known for treating the desperate, but never without demanding payment first.
When Kai arrived, he explained the situation quickly.
"Necrosis, huh..."
Chrisome’s eyes squinted behind the mask he had just worn.
"I’ll do my best... But before I can give you assurance, I need to see her directly and run some tests."
"Alright... We can do that." Kai replied.
"Great! As for the payment..."
Just like that, Chrisome agreed to come, but only after Kai placed ten C‐Grade cores on the counter for the advance.
The physician’s gloved hands scooped them up without hesitation, and he followed Kai back through the winding streets.
Inside, Chrisome moved like it was his home.
He even knelt beside Xinyi... Thanks to his mask, it filtered the stench of rot, and he pressed two fingers against her wrist.
"Let’s see..."

His brow furrowed as he checked her pulse, then shifted his hand to her neck. The silence in the room lasted for some time as he examined her arm, lifting it slightly. The blackened flesh was already stiff and lifeless.

"This is advanced necrosis," Chrisome said flatly. "The corruption has already taken the limb. If it spreads further, she won’t last." He straightened and shook his head... "The only option is removal. Amputation... But I’m not an expert on that matter. There could be side effects if I operate."
Xian’s face went pale, his hands trembling as he looked between his sister and the physician. "Then... do it. Please."
Chrisome raised a hand, stopping him. "Payment first. An additional 30 C‐Grade cores. That is the price for the procedure."

The demand lasted for a few moments before Kai wryly smiled. He had already paid ten just to bring the man here, and now the physician was asking for more... far more than most slum families could ever afford.
Farrah and Mei could only sigh at the situation.
They had seen this before... physicians who treated survival as business, not mercy.
Kai finally spoke, deciding to take this matter into his own hands. "Enough. You can leave now."
Chrisome blinked, surprised at the reaction, but when Kai gestured toward the door, he gathered his bag and left without another word.
The sound of his boots faded down the alley, leaving only silence behind.
Finally, Kai turned back to Xinyi... "We’ll handle this ourselves. Trust me."
He then looked at Xian and the others...
Since the physician couldn’t heal her, amputation was an obvious answer.
"My solution is simple. Give her sedatives. Then, we cut the arm cleanly and heal it with my Hemostatic Vial. After that, we use the Arm Replacement Implant."
"Ahhh... I think I know about that. I didn’t expect you to purchase one." Mei commented as she saw the Arm Replacement Implant from the Gene Trader before.
"But how about the pain? I don’t think that will be comfortable." Farrah asked curiously.
But Kai just smiled. "I’ll handle that with my Medic Gift Pack..."
He then turned to the patient.
"For now, I need to ask you, Xinyi... Is it okay to replace your left arm with a machine?" Kai asked.

chapters.title: Chapter 257: Operation
paragraphs: Chrisome’s departure had solidified Kai’s resolve...
After all, he knew that this could happen with his friends and Guild Members as well.
He had to prepare for situations like this, even if he hadn’t expected them to come so soon.
’This should be fine...’

The Arm Replacement Implant was his ace. He had acquired it from Terrence, a man who had once been a reliable member of the shelter until he obtained a skill that controls the mind of other Survivors.

In any case, before the man left, Kai had claimed the black metal box that was basically the implant. It wasn’t just a prosthetic... it was a system‐linked device capable of synchronizing with the patient, adjusting its functions to the user’s body weight, age, and even combat style.
Then there was the Hemostatic Vial.

Kai remembered looting it from Alex, a Survivor who had underestimated his strength. The vial was rare, designed to stop bleeding instantly by accelerating clotting and sealing wounds at the cellular level. It was the kind of tool that could mean the difference between life and death in battlefield surgery.
And finally, his Medical Gift Pack.
Needless to say, he wouldn’t be using the Basic or the Enhanced Gift Pack. He would use a superior grade instead.
Inside were various items, including an Advanced Surgical Kit and Trauma Kit, among many others.
The Surgical Kit contained many sterilized items, including the local anesthetic injectors, calibrated to deliver exact doses depending on the patient’s weight and age.
The Trauma Kit also carried painkiller injectors, equally measured, with a guide etched into the case to ensure no mistakes were made.
Kai’s plan was clear.

He would sedate Xinyi, amputate the necrotic arm cleanly, stop the bleeding with the Hemostatic Vial, and then activate the Arm Replacement Implant. It was brutal, but it was the only way to save her... and perhaps, it could also save the other people who might need the same treatment.
"Is it okay to replace your left arm with a machine?" Kai asked softly.
Xinyi was weak, but she knew that this was a good opportunity.
Although she was already happy if she could just remove the sick arm, she would be grateful!
Soon, she finally managed to whisper, "Yes."
That single word was enough...
They couldn’t do this in the open. Kai opened a Basic Shelter Gift Pack and pulled out a small collapsible tent.
Within minutes, they had set up a sterile environment, as clean as the slums would allow.
The tent’s reinforced fabric muffled the sounds outside, creating a safe space...
Then, Kai paused as he arranged the instruments... He remembered something else he had kept hidden away for emergencies. From his pack, he pulled out a small vial filled with a golden liquid.
Mei’s eyes widened immediately, and Farrah nodded in recognition. They knew exactly what it was.
"Alpha Gene Enhancement Serum..." Mei whispered.
But Xinyi and Xian had no clue. They stared at the vial, uncertain, while Kai smiled faintly. He tilted the vial carefully, letting the liquid catch the dim light of the tent.
"This will help," Kai said simply.
He drew out a dropper and measured four drops, placing them gently on Xinyi’s lips. She swallowed weakly, and within moments, her breathing steadied.
A faint warmth spread through her body, with color returning to her cheeks. The serum was working, strengthening her from within!

Still, Kai knew it wasn’t enough. The necrosis wouldn’t vanish just because of the serum. The rotting arm was beyond saving. But at least her body had gained resilience, enough to endure what was coming.
"You will be working for us soon," Kai said, turning toward Xian. His tone was firm, but not unkind. "So you’ll have ten drops."
Xian’s eyes widened... It seemed that his fate was already sealed.

Soon, his hands trembled as he accepted the serum. Thankfully, Mei assisted him. She steadied the boy, guiding the dropper to his mouth. He swallowed the golden liquid, and almost instantly, his body reacted.
His Spirit surged, his eyes brightened, and he felt strength he had never known before.
Nonetheless, Kai didn’t linger on their reactions. He was already prepping.
The anesthetic injector was calibrated precisely for Xinyi’s frail weight, while the trauma kit’s painkiller injector was readied as backup.
"Alright... Let’s start."
Just like that, the operation began.
First, the injection went in smoothly, and soon, Xinyi’s breathing slowed, her body relaxing as the sedative took hold.
Kai’s hands moved swiftly...
They had killed before, cut through flesh and bone in battles against both men and machines. He wasn’t new to this...
Soon, the knife sliced cleanly. Her rotting arm was severed in one decisive motion. There was no scream... only silence.
Blood welled instantly, but Kai was quick... He uncorked the Hemostatic Vial and poured its contents over the wound.
"Mhmm... This should work... if not..." Kai muttered as he prepared to use his backup from the Trauma Kit...
Thankfully, the effect was immediate... the bleeding slowed, then stopped entirely, the tissue was sealed under the vial’s chemical reaction.
Just like that, the tent smelled of iron and medicine. The blackened arm lay discarded, lifeless, while Xinyi kept breathing steadily...
"Next..." Kai muttered as Mei handed over the black metal box.
It was the Arm Replacement Implant.
He pressed the activation switch, and the device hummed to life.
Clink... Clink...
Panels slid open as mechanical joints unfolded...
Soon, the implant latched onto the severed shoulder with its connectors piercing gently into flesh.
The system responded.
Sensors calibrated to her body weight and age adjusted the implant’s framework.

Motors engaged, gears were aligned, and the skeletal frame extended outward. Piece by piece, the arm assembled itself... metal plates locking into place, wiring threading through the structure, synthetic muscle fibers also started forming...
"Whoa... So this is how it works." Kai muttered.
"This is worth 14 Survivor Medals, right?" Mei muttered.
"It’s worth the price..." Farrah nodded.
Minutes passed, and the arm was complete.
A mechanical limb that was black and polished was now Xinyi’s new left arm!
"Xinyi... Y-you have an arm now..."

chapters.title: Chapter 258: The New Arm, the Faction, and the Quota
paragraphs: Kai knew Xinyi needed more rest despite consuming the serum...
So after the operation, they returned to the Silver Rest Inn and rented a room for the two siblings.

They bought new clothes from a nearby stall, simple but clean, and let the children wash up. Mei carefully wiped Xinyi down, avoiding her left shoulder while Xian took a proper bath. Soon after, both of them collapsed onto the bed, sleeping like logs.
Later that night, Mei sat across from Kai...
"Are you really going to take care of them?"
Kai shook his head.
"No. I don’t have to take care of them. They should be strong enough to work for us. Shelter life isn’t about pity... it’s about survival. They’ll help clean, do chores, and earn their place."
As long as their Health Points return to their peak, then they should be just fine.
Mei frowned slightly, but Kai continued.
"Don’t forget Xian’s title.Scrap Survivor.That’s super valuable... He could become our scavenger unit leader. With that title, he’ll be able to find and repurpose junk better than anyone else."
He glanced at Xinyi, sleeping soundly with her new arm. "And her... that arm isn’t just a replacement. It’s adaptive, right? It can be used for combat...
They all knew that as she grew, the implant would also adjust and expand with her body. She’ would be an asset too.
The next morning, Kai didn’t give her time to rest. He pulled out the golden vial again... the Alpha Gene Enhancement Serum and measured another drop.
"Have another one..." he said simply.

Xinyi obeyed, and the moment the serum touched her tongue, strength surged through her body. She sat up and felt the energy that she thought she could never have. "Thank you... Sir Kai, everyone... thank you."
Then, her first question was hesitant. "Where... where’s my arm? The one you cut off?"
Claire, who had joined them, answered plainly.
"It was burnt. No trace left... Do you want to see it?"
Xinyi smiled faintly and shook her head... "No... It’s good. I don’t want to see it again."
Then, she flexed her new mechanical arm, testing its movement.
The fingers curled, the joints rotated smoothly, and the synthetic muscles responded to her...
She tried lifting a chair, then opening and closing her hand repeatedly. Kai and the others let her experiment freely, watching her adapt.
Well, they were also curious about this new arm after all...
They gave the siblings food once more, simple bread and stew, and told them to stay at the inn. "Rest here. We’ll be back," Kai instructed.
Then Kai, Mei, and Farrah left together.
Their destination was already planned last night... the Aries Faction.
Cornelio’s invitation token had to be tested.
When they arrived, Kai and the others were surprised to see a long line stretching outside the Aries Faction’s gates.
The crowd wasn’t ragged beggars or refugees... they looked determined, some even dressed in decent gear.
Kai frowned. "Strange. They’re not here for food or shelter, right?"
As they moved closer, snippets of conversation reached them.
"Six months of service, that’s all it takes," one man whispered to his companion.
"Work for the Aries Faction, and they’ll give you the Gene Skill Crystal forStrong Spiritfor free."
Another group nearby spoke calmly... "Forget waiting six months. If you’ve got fifty B‐Grade Cores, you can buy one outright. But only forty are sold each month. That’s why everyone’s lining up."
Mei tilted her head, listening carefully. "So that’s what this is about... not food or protection. They’re here for skill crystals."
Farrah’s eyes narrowed. "Strong Spirit."
"I wonder what’s so special about that?"

A woman in line heard their conversation and muttered. "With Strong Spirit, you can attempt Skill Fusion with two other rare Gene Skills. If you succeed, you getHardened Spirit.That’s the real prize... It boosts defense and Spirit endurance... and many others. Everyone wants it, it’s practically a ticket to survival."
Mei’s eyes widened. This was their first time learning about the possible recipe for a Skill Fusion.
"So Strong Spirit is one of the prerequisites... and Hardened Spirit is the fused skill."
Kai’s mind clicked instantly. He remembered Cornelio.
’Cornelio had a Hardened Spirit at Level 7. That explains it. No wonder this is sought after.’
"So that’s the deal. Six months of service, or fifty B‐Grade Cores. Either way, the Aries Faction controls access. And they’re limiting supply to forty crystals a month."
Mei glanced at him. "That explains the crowd..."
Kai smirked. "Cornelio’s invitation token might be worth more than we thought..."
The three of them stood quietly for a moment, listening to the chatter ripple through the crowd.
Soon, they found one of the guards and approached him while showing the invitation.
The Aries Faction guard eyed them as they approached.
"We’re here to enter." Kai said as he handed the token to the guard.

The guard’s brows furrowed. He took the token, inspected it closely, and then his expression shifted... He recognized this token and this wasn’t just a normal one. It must’ve been provided by one of the elders or even higher.
"This is genuine." He muttered, and the nearby people turned their heads.
The crowd stirred immediately.
"An invitation token?
"Who are they?"
"Wait... they’re not waiting in line?"
The guard straightened, and his tone changed to a respectful one. "You don’t need to wait in line. Follow me."
Gasps and whispers broke out behind them. Some people protested.
"Hey! We’ve been waiting for hours!"
"Why do they get to skip?"
"Unfair!"

chapters.title: Chapter 259: The VR World’s Entry and the Ore
paragraphs: Kai, Mei, and Farrah were still unsure about this VR World. They have already heard the Perfect World numerous times since yesterday.
Perhaps it was already time to learn more about this place.
"Are we going to get paid for our work?. Since Cornelio wasn’t here yet, they might as well take this opportunity to safely learn about the VR World.
"Yes! There’s a payment! You will receive it after..."
Kai nodded as he was slowly being convinced. Furthermore, it wasn’t like there was a VR Café in this city where they could just enter and use the Pods for a certain price per hour.

Perhaps, entering Perfect World under the Aries Faction’s guidance might reveal more about their systems, their resources, and the way they produced the coveted Skill Crystals that he heard from the people outside.
Kai asked once again. "Four hours, you say?"

Maya nodded quickly. "Yes. Four hours in the mines... There should be 30-minute breaks. It won’t interfere with your meeting with Cornelio. By the time you’re done, he should be back. I remember that you will earn two to five C-Grade Energy Cores depending on your performance."

Maya then continued explaining the benefits it would give to them... The free items, the training, the free unlock of the location, the relationship to their Faction, and many other perks they could obtain.
Kai glanced at Mei and Farrah. Both gave subtle nods.
"Alright," Kai said at last. "Show us the way."
"Yes!"
Maya heaved a sigh of relief, finally feeling the pressure ease from her shoulders.
"Good... you don’t know how much this helps," she muttered, then gestured for them to follow.
She led Kai, Mei, and Farrah down a corridor lined with banners of the Aries Faction until they reached a wide chamber.
At this point, they had already introduced themselves to each other.
"We’re here, Kai..." Maya muttered.
The air inside was cool as they probably had to maintain the temperature of the VR Pods.

Soon, they saw the VR Hall stretched before them... rows upon rows of polished pods arranged in perfect symmetry. More than sixty pods stood in line. Without a doubt, these pods were the third-generation version.
Kai recalled that it had adaptive comfort systems, advanced neural synchronization, optimized energy usage, and many other features.
"Whoa..."
"This looks cool."
"You must really trust these things. I wonder how you can all feel confident that the A.I. Civilization wouldn’t hack into this thing."
The three of them were simply amazed.
Fifty of them were already occupied. It was obvious from the faint pulses of light flickering across their surfaces as users remained connected.
Then, ten pods sat open with their hatches lifted, waiting for new entrants.
Kai studied them carefully.
Each pod was large enough to hold a person comfortably, with padded interiors and a single cable running into the walls for each pod...
The faint hum of machinery filled the hall, accompanied by the occasional beep of monitoring devices.
Maya cupped her hands around her mouth and called out... "Bart! I need you here!"
At the far end of the hall, a man looked up from a chessboard.
He was tall, with rolled-up sleeves and grease stains on his uniform. Across from him sat another man dressed in white robes, clearly a medic.
This man didn’t look at the group as he studied the board.
Bart, on the other hand, groaned and pushed his chair back.
"Always when I’m about to win..." He stood, brushing off his hands, and walked toward them.
Maya quickly explained the situation.
"These three will be entering Perfect World for four hours. They’re new, so I need you to handle the connection process."
Bart nodded, his demeanor shifted to a professional one. "Alright. Let me explain how this works." He gestured toward the nearest open pod.

"Here’s how it works. Once you lie down, the pod closes and connects to your neural signals. The system calibrates your vitals, then boots you into Perfect World’s login interface. That’s where you’ll create your character. Name, appearance, and your starting attributes... all of that is chosen before you enter the world itself. No one spawns without finishing that step."

He chuckled with his own joke before he tapped the pod’s side. "After creation, you’ll spawn in Beginner Town... Lyria. Everyone starts there. It’s crowded with new players, merchants, and guides. Don’t get distracted. The town is designed to orient newcomers, but you’ll want to head straight to the Aries contact."
Mei leaned forward. "Who do we look for?"

Bart nodded. "There’s a liaison named Dalen stationed near the training grounds in Lyria. He handles Aries recruits. Once you speak to him, he’ll register your character under the faction and arrange transport to the Aries mining site. That’s where you’ll be working."
Farrah frowned. "So we’ll have to walk through the town first?"

Bart smirked. "Exactly. Think of it as a tutorial. You’ll see the bustle of Perfect World... players trading, training, forming parties. It’s overwhelming at first, but it gives you a sense of scale...Just 15 minutes would do. Once you reach Dalen, he’ll send you by caravan to the Aries restricted zone. The mines are located in the foothills outside their territory. You’ll probably arrive there in another 15 minutes..."

He then grew serious. "Inside the mines, you’ll be given basic gear... pickaxes, ore sacks, and a map. Your job is to collect mystic iron ore. After you’re done, you will hand over the sack to the officer outside the mine. Anyway, you’ll earn C‐Grade Energy Cores based on performance."
Kai studied the pods and gently nodded... "So it’s character creation, then Lyria, then Dalen, then the mines."

Bart nodded firmly. "That’s the path. And remember... Perfect World feels real. Pain, fatigue, and even exhaustion register. But don’t panic. If anything goes wrong, the pod forces a disconnect. That’s why I’m here, and why the medic watches your vitals."
"Ahh? Real pain? Wait a moment... Isn’t this a game?" Mei repeated as she thought that it wouldn’t be too troublesome for them to work.

But Bart gave a slow nod. "Yes. Not the kind that leaves scars, but enough to remind you that actions have weight here... Swinging a pickaxe for hours will tire your arms. If a rock falls, you’ll feel the impact. It’s part of the immersion. Without it, people would treat Perfect World like a toy. Well, it’s not like we can control the Perfect World’s settings. Still, with the Third Gen pods, you’d get to easily use your skills once your body got scanned."
"Ahh... So it was like that." Kai gently nodded.
Farrah still frowned at this as she felt uneasy. "So exhaustion, strain... even injuries register?"

The medic, who had been silent until now, finally spoke. His voice was calm and reassured them. "You won’t get injured. It’s all about the mind... Still, that’s why I’m here. The pods monitor your vitals constantly. If your body shows signs of overload...too much stress, pain, or Spirit drain, the system forces a disconnect. You’ll wake up here, safe. Think of it as training wheels. The danger feels real, but it’s controlled. Don’t worry... The mine is pretty much safe unless the place collapses..."
Kai nodded. "So it’s harsh, but not reckless."

Bart smirked. "Exactly. It’s designed to push you... You might even get bonus stats while mining. It’s one of the safest place to increase your endurance. Furthermore, for newcomers, the faction keeps things simple. Mining duty is straightforward. You’ll get breaks every thirty minutes, and the work is monitored. If you collapse in the VR world, the pod pulls you out before anything serious happens. But again, you won’t work there until you collapse."
Mei exhaled slowly, her concern easing.
"That... actually makes sense. If Perfect World is meant to be used as a training ground, then feeling the strain is part of it."
Farrah still looked skeptical, but she gave a reluctant nod. "At least they’re not throwing us into combat right away."

Maya, who had been listening intently, smiled faintly. "That’s why the arrangement is perfect for you three. You’re new, and the mines are safe compared to the battlefields. You’ll learn how the world feels, how your bodies respond, and you’ll earn cores while waiting for Cornelio. It’s a fair start. After all, you will lose your login rights for 24 hours once you die inside."
"Oh? You can’t login one full day if you’re killed inside?" Kai asked.
"That’s right..." Maya replied with a smile.
Kai nodded as he glanced at the pods again.
He understood that it was indeed one of the safest ways to step into Perfect World without risking his life in combat zones.
"Alright," Kai said finally. "We’re fine working for a few hours to experience it... If this is how Perfect World works, then we’ll learn it properly."
Bart grinned, satisfied. "Good. That’s the right attitude. Now, let’s get you connected."
As he said this, one VR Pod opened up, and it wasn’t an alarming situation.
Whoosh~
The hatch of the pod nearby lifted, and a man in his twenties smiled as soon as he saw the group.
He was filled with excitement!
"Haha! I found a Mithril Ore, Sir Bart, Miss Maya!"

You’re new, and the mines are safe compared to the battlefields.
You’ll learn how the world feels, how your bodies respond, and you’ll earn cores while waiting for Cornelio.
It’s a fair start.
After all, you will lose your login rights for 24 hours once you die inside."
"Oh?
You can’t login one full day if you’re killed inside?" Kai asked.
"That’s right..." Maya replied with a smile.
Kai nodded as he glanced at the pods again.
He understood that it was indeed one of the safest ways to step into Perfect World without risking his life in combat zones.
"Alright," Kai said finally.
"We’re fine working for a few hours to experience it...
If this is how Perfect World works, then we’ll learn it properly."
Bart grinned, satisfied.
"Good.
That’s the right attitude.
Now, let’s get you connected."
As he said this, one VR Pod opened up, and it wasn’t an alarming situation.
Whoosh~
The hatch of the pod nearby lifted, and a man in his twenties smiled as soon as he saw the group.
He was filled with excitement!
"Haha!
I found a Mithril Ore, Sir Bart, Miss Maya!"

chapters.title: Chapter 260: Perfect World
paragraphs: A few moments ago, Kai still had doubts gnawing at him.
He worried not about the dangers inside Perfect World, but about what might happen outside. What if someone tried to rob them while their minds were connected?
What if the worst came to pass while they were defenseless in the pods?
He even considered sending Mei and Farrah in while he stayed behind to guard them.

But seeing the young man emerge from the pod, grinning with excitement as he announced his discovery, Kai felt his mind ease. The man’s joy was genuine, his excitement was unrestrained. It reassured Kai that this arrangement was safe enough... the Aries Faction clearly had guards, staff, and systems in place to protect their people.
Furthermore, they were really curious about the VR World.
Kai himself was still weighing whether to purchase the Neural Gear for 100 Reputation Points.
"Haha! I found a Mithril Ore, Sir Bart, Miss Maya!" the man exclaimed.
Bart’s eyes lit up. "Mithril? That’s incredible! Do you know how rare that is? You’re the first one to collect that ore this year!"

The medic leaned back, smiling faintly. "The elders will be pleased. With Mithril, they can forge another high‐grade sword. Maybe even strong enough to challenge the hidden dungeon on the sixth floor."
Maya clapped her hands together as she felt relieved hearing that... "You’re amazing, Troy... This is perfect timing. The mining teams have been struggling, but this will change everything."
Kai frowned slightly, confused. "Floors? What do you mean?"
He said this softly, but still, he was heard by the others.

Bart chuckled, realizing the newcomers had no idea. "Perfect World isn’t just a flat map. It’s layered... floors stacked one above the other. Each floor is harder than the last, filled with stronger monsters, rarer resources, and harsher conditions. Most players never make it past the fourth. The sixth floor is infamous. Only factions with elite equipment and skills dare to challenge it."
Mei’s eyes widened while Farrah took note of everything they were saying.

Kai also stayed silent, absorbing the information. He didn’t understand the full scope yet, but he knew enough... Perfect World wasn’t just a training ground. It was vast, structured, and dangerous in ways he hadn’t imagined.

Bart continued with his voice filled with pride. "That’s why Mithril matters. It’s one of the few ores that can be refined into weapons or equipment capable of enduring the certain dungeon or floor’s trials. As you can see, every piece mined is celebrated. And you three, even if you don’t get anything other than the mystic iron ore, that’s perfectly fine.
Kai nodded slowly...
He didn’t fully grasp the mechanics of these "floors," but he understood that they were dangerous.
Kai glanced at Mei and Farrah. They were silent, but he could tell they were absorbing every word, just as he was.
Soon, they were finally allowed to enter the VR World.
Kai climbed into the pod, the padded interior adjusting instantly to his weight.
Then, the hatch slid shut with a hiss, sealing him in darkness.
For a moment, he felt his chest tighten... this was the point of no return. Then the hum of machinery surrounded him, and a cascade of lights appeared across his vision...
[Neural synchronization initializing...Scanning vitals...Spirit resonance detected.
Gene Skill compatibility confirmed.Adaptive comfort engaged.]
A tingling sensation spread across his body, as though every nerve was being mapped. Kai clenched his fists, forcing himself to stay calm.
[Avatar creation unlocked.
Note: Appearance locked to genetic scan for skill synchronization.Customization limited to name selection.]

Kai nodded... So he couldn’t change his appearance. It made sense... if Perfect World allowed them to use their real gene skills, then the system had to keep avatars aligned with their scanned bodies in order for them to accurately use their skills.
The interface then appeared before his eyes.
[ Character Creation ]
Enter Avatar Name:
Kai hesitated. He didn’t want to use his real name. This was a new world, a new identity should also follow.
Slowly, he typed: "Ashen."
[ Name confirmed: Ashen. ]
[ Avatar creation complete. ]
The darkness shifted, and suddenly a cinematic began to play...
A ruined city appeared first... skyscrapers were toppled, streets had webbing cracks, flames could be seen in various places as if the town was just bombarded by artillery...
But then, alien warships hovered above, their hulls filled with strange weapons.
The narration then echoed in Kai’s ears...

"Perfect World was born from humanity’s last stand. Alien races invaded, corrupting the land and mutating animals into monstrous beasts. Humanity gathered its survivors, forging factions, and built this layered world to fight back. Twelve floors rise above us. Each floor is a battlefield. At the top lies the alien core. Only by destroying it can humanity reclaim its future."

The images shifted... mutated wolves, tigers, condors, even large worms appeared in forests and cities while insectoid aliens tore through barricades of shelters as they ordered colossal beasts to rampage everywhere...
Kai appreciated this introduction. At least now he knew what kind of enemies awaited inside... mutated beasts twisted by alien influence, and the aliens themselves.
The narration continued, allowing them to learn that the first and second floors were dangerous, but they were still basically training grounds for all the players to level up.
Kai exhaled slowly as he understood the situation now.
[ Spawn point: Beginner Town - Lyra. ]
Light engulfed him, and the world opened.
Cobblestone streets stretched out, lined with wooden stalls and bustling players.
Merchants were everywhere, while adventurers were moving about...
"Whoa... It feels real..."
It was far more vivid than Kai expected. He then blinked for a few times, adjusting to the brightness.
A moment later, two flashes of light appeared beside him.
Mei and Farrah spawned in, their avatars identical to their real selves...
Mei’s eyes widened. "So this is Lyra..."
Farrah crossed her arms, scanning the crowd. "It feels... real. Too real."

Kai nodded slowly. He glanced around, absorbing everything... the chatter of players forming parties, the sight of trainers giving free combat lessons, and the smell of bread wafting from a nearby stall.
"Alright... Let’s find that Dalen." Mei said.
However, Kai shook his head.
"No... We have to do something first."

chapters.title: Chapter 261: The Beginner’s Town
paragraphs: Kai raised his hand, stopping Mei before she could rush off.
"No... we have to do something first."
Mei tilted her head. "What should we do first?"
Kai nodded firmly. "Check your status. We need to know what we’re working with before we meet anyone."
Just like that, the three of them opened their system menus, translucent windows appearing before their eyes.
[ Character Status
Name: Ashen
Titles: None
Level: 1
Health: 100 / 100
Energy: 50 / 50
Physique Rating: F+
Strength: 10
Intelligence: 10
Dexterity: 10
Endurance: 10
Vitality: 10
Reputation: 0
Faction: None ]
Kai gently nodded after seeing this. It was indeed a basic stat.
"Level one... base stats. Just like starting from scratch."
Mei and Farrah confirmed similar numbers... Their health and energy values weren’t different. Basically, everyone had the same starting point.
It was quite interesting since they immediately felt the difference in being weaker.
In the real world, they had already grown stronger through training and gene enhancements, but here, Perfect World reset them to the baseline.
Farrah tapped another tab. "Inventory."
A new window appeared:
[ Inventory ]
[ Slot 1: Newbie Gift Pack ]
[ Slot 2-10: Empty ]
Mei’s eyes sparkled. "We even get starter items." She tapped the pack, and a description appeared:
[ Newbie Gift Pack ]
[ Contains: Basic rations, beginner weapon voucher, 5 healing salves, 1 stamina potion. ]
The voucher would actually help them select their first weapon. It could be a stick, a short sword, a spear, a dagger, or other basic weapons they could choose from.
Kai nodded. "That’s useful. At least they don’t throw us empty-handed."
Finally, he opened the Skill Tab. His eyes widened.
[ Active Skills: Spirit Pulse Lv0, Specter Step Lv0, Fast Appraisal Lv0, Beast Arm Lv0 ]
[ Passive Skills: Keen Sense Lv0, Bio Adaptive Constitution Lv0, Battle Trance Lv0, Bronze Skin Lv0 ]
Kai couldn’t help but smile at this...
"Our gene skills... they’re here."
Mei gasped as she checked her own tab. "Mine too! But... all at level zero."
Farrah frowned. "So they don’t carry over our real‐world progress. Still, it’s impressive that Perfect World recognizes them at all."

Kai studied the list carefully. Spirit Pulse, Specter Step, Fast Appraisal, Beast Arm... all the abilities he had relied on before, now displayed here, even if locked at Lv0. The passive skills were there too... Keen Sense, Bio‐Adaptive Constitution, Battle Trance, Bronze Skin. Their descriptions were intact, waiting to be mastered again.

He clenched his fists, feeling a surge of excitement. "This Perfect World is just too mysterious. I wonder who made this thing. The pod really scanned us, and now our gene skills exist here too. Even if they start at zero, we can grow them inside this world."
Mei smiled faintly. "Maybe training here strengthens us both ways... in the VR world and maybe even outside."

Farrah crossed her arms, still cautious but intrigued. "If that’s true, then that would explain why the factions invest so much in mining and exploration. If skills can evolve here, then Perfect World is just too valuable."
Kai closed the menu, his doubts fading.
He finally understood why Bart had said the mines were safe yet meaningful. Even simple tasks like mining could raise endurance, unlock stat bonuses, and strengthen their skills.
He looked at Mei and Farrah. "Alright. Now we know where we stand. Level one, base stats, starter pack, and our gene skills waiting to grow. This is our foundation."
Mei nodded. "Then let’s move forward."
Farrah glanced at the bustling streets of Lyra. "And find Dalen."
Kai smirked. "Exactly..."
The three of them made their way through the bustling streets of Lyra, moving past merchants and adventurers until the noise gave way to a wide training ground.
Wooden dummies lined the area, and recruits sparred while being watched by some instructors.
At the far end stood a man in a simple but sturdy shirt, the Aries Faction logo stitched proudly across the chest.
"That must be him," Kai said quietly.
Mei nodded. "Dalen."
They approached, and the man turned...
"You three... Maya just sent a private message. Do you have the code?"
Kai stepped forward, recalling the phrase Maya had whispered before they left. "Iron sings when struck."
Dalen’s expression eased into a smile. "Good. That confirms it... and remember that phrase. Anyway, you’re organized to be here."
He gestured toward a small carriage waiting nearby.
"Come. We’ll head to the mining site."
The ride was steady but long, the wheels clattered against cobblestone before shifting to dirt paths.
For twenty minutes, they traveled past rolling hills and sparse forests until the carriage slowed before a cave entrance.
"Mhhmm?" Kai was curious since at the mouth of the cave was a strange rippling wave like water...
"What is that?" Mei asked.
Dalen explained calmly.
"The entry barrier. Only level five and below can pass through. It keeps the higher‐ranked players out, ensures the mines remain for recruits and trainees."
As if to confirm his words, a notification appeared before their eyes:
[ Entry restriction detected. Only Level 5 and below permitted. ]
Kai nodded. "It matches."
Dalen handed each of them a bundle.
"Here. Equipment for the job."
Kai opened his pack... a miner’s hat, a sturdy pickaxe, a reinforced ore sack, a folded map of the tunnels, and a simple lunch box with rations. Mei and Farrah received the same.
"Use the map to avoid getting lost," Dalen instructed. "The foreman will guide you further. His name is Jules. He’s strict, but fair."
Kai tightened his grip on the pickaxe. "Understood."
Together, the three stepped through the rippling barrier.
The sensation was strange... like walking through a curtain of liquid, but it vanished as quickly as it came.
Inside, the cavern appeared, and it was huge, unlike what they had seen outside!
It was also lit by glowing crystals embedded in the walls.
Clang! Clang! Clang!
The sound of metal striking stone echoed faintly. At the center stood a broad‐shouldered man with a miner’s helmet and a clipboard in hand.
He looked up as they approached. "New recruits?"
