chapters.title: Chapter 262: The Mines and Cornelio
paragraphs: At this point, Kai and the other two had already gotten used to the different atmosphere within the Virtual World.
It just felt like reality, and as a matter of fact, it even felt slightly better to be moving around here.
At this time, Jules lowered his clipboard as he studied the three of them. "New recruits?"
Mei nodded. "Yes. We were sent by Dalen. We’re here to work temporarily..."
The foreman gave a curt nod.

"Good. Then listen carefully. The mines aren’t complicated, but they demand discipline. You’ll be swinging pickaxes for hours, and if you don’t pace yourselves, fatigue will cripple you before you’ve filled a single sack."
He gestured toward the glowing crystals embedded in the walls. Their light glowed across veins of darker stone, where faint metallic glints peeked through.

"That’s mystic iron ore. Your job is to extract it cleanly. Strike too hard, and you’ll shatter the vein, wasting the resource. Strike too soft, and you’ll get nothing. But don’t worry too much about the output... Even if Level 1 is normally the luckiest one, the success rate is low for everyone... Just chill." Jules said with a nonchalant voice as if this job wasn’t too important.
Kai couldn’t help but smile after noticing how carefree he was.
Just like what Maya said, this was indeed a simple task that could help them get used to the gameplay before playing the VR World seriously.
Soon, a notification appeared before their eyes:
[ Mining Mechanics ]
- Stamina decreases with each swing.
- Proper timing increases yield.
- Overexertion causes fatigue penalties.
- Ore sacks auto‐register collected units.
With this much information, they only need to learn which spot they should start digging.
Mei tilted her head, intrigued.
"So it’s not just brute force mining... There’s a rhythm to it... I guess this is really just a game, huh..."
Jules nodded.

"Exactly. Mining here is just a game. You’ll feel a pulse in the pickaxe when you strike correctly. That pulse means the system has registered a clean hit. Chain enough of those, and your yield multiplies."
"What if we’re not doing it right?" Farrah asked.

"Nothing... You waste stamina and time," Jules said bluntly. "But don’t worry... we’re not expecting much. We just need more miners to increase our chances of finding ores. Alright. That’s enough explanation."
He motioned toward a group of miners further down the cavern. They swung in steady rhythm, their pickaxes glowing faintly with each impact.
The sound of metal against stone echoed like a heartbeat.
Every few minutes, one of them paused to empty fragments into their ore sack, the system seemed to be tallying the weight automatically.
Kai tightened his grip on his pickaxe and was quite curious how this would work.
As they started walking to the spot they had to mine, Jules explained the map they had obtained.

"The tunnels branch in three directions. Left is shallow veins... easy to mine, but low yield. The center is balanced with moderate difficulty, but decent rewards. Right is deeper veins... It’s harder to strike, but the ore is purer. You can choose your own spots. Most recruits start in the center."
Kai exchanged a glance with Mei and Farrah. "We’ll start in the center."

Jules nodded approvingly. "Smart choice. Remember, mining also builds your stats. If you mine enough, it won’t be surprising if you gain bonus Strength, Endurance, or Dexterity Stat... Very well, make sure to always wear your hat..."
Just like that, the three of them stepped toward the central tunnel. There were glowing crystals around, and nine other miners were also stationed here.
These people didn’t bother the three newcomers. It seemed that they were already used to having new people every now and then.
Soon, Kai raised his pickaxe and swung...
Clang!
The metal rang against stone, but nothing happened. No vibration, no notification.
He tried again.
Clang!
Still nothing. The pickaxe felt heavy and awkward in his hands. The rhythm Jules had mentioned seemed like a beat he couldn’t catch.
Minutes passed as Kai, Mei and Farrah kept swinging... Each strike echoed through the cavern, but nothing was happening.
Sweat beaded on his forehead, his stamina bar ticking down little by little. Mei and Farrah glanced at him, their own attempts were also producing similar failures.
Kai gritted his teeth. "So it’s not that easy..."
He steadied himself, recalling Jules’s words about timing.
He waited, feeling for the faint pulse in the handle... He swung again...
Clang!
It seemed it was too early. The pickaxe scraped uselessly against stone.
Another swing... too late. The vibration slipped past him.
"Ugh... I’m not good with rhythm-based games." Kai frowned.
Finally, after several failed attempts, he caught it.
The pickaxe struck at the right moment...
A notification appeared before his eyes.
[ Clean Hit Registered ]
[ You have obtained 1 Mystic Iron Ore ]
In the meantime, just as Kai, Mei, and Farrah were getting used to the VR World, Cornelio Aries strode back into the Aries Faction compound...

At this time, his boots were dusty from travel, and a unique sword was strapped across his back. The weapon was unlike anything forged by human hands. It had sleek lines, strange alloys, and faintly glowing circuits etched into the blade.
Apparently, it was a sword and a gun fused together.
He had taken it from an A-Rank Unit of the A.I. Army during his mission, and even now, his eyes lingered on its craftsmanship, fascinated by the technology the A.I. civilization wielded.
Maya spotted him immediately, and she was shocked...
"Sir Cornelio? You’re back already? I thought you’d arrive in a few more hours."
Cornelio chuckled as he also thought the same. "The mission ended sooner than expected. But tell me... I heard we had visitors?"
Maya hesitated. "Yes. The ones you gave an invitation token. They’re here. I... sent them to the mines."
Cornelio blinked, then let out a laugh...
"Oh? He’s finally here, and you sent him to mine? You..." He rubbed his forehead, torn between amusement and exasperation.

Still, his expression softened. "Perhaps it’s for the best. The Perfect World holds secrets tied to the Anima civilization... I plan to introduce it to them, so I guess this experience will help them to understand my words easily."

Left is shallow veins... easy to mine, but low yield.
The center is balanced with moderate difficulty, but decent rewards.
Right is deeper veins...
It’s harder to strike, but the ore is purer.
You can choose your own spots.
Most recruits start in the center."

chapters.title: Chapter 263: The Anima’s Secret Goal and the Trade
paragraphs: Cornelio relaxed as he leaned against the stone wall of the Aries Faction reception hall.
His hand was resting on the strange sword strapped across his back. The weapon was still warm, reminding him of the battle he had just endured.

Soon, his mind drifted to the secrets they had uncovered in past missions... They were information that the elders had already mentioned before, but because there wasn’t any evidence, they weren’t taken that seriously.
However, after raiding another A.I. Base, he confirmed that the Perfect World was not just a training ground or a simulation for Survivors like them...
It was a domain that Anima, the A.I. civilization, had been trying to seize for years.
Anima had twisted Aria, once humanity’s proud creation, into a rebel force. Through Aria, they had betrayed humanity, turning machines into enemies.
But apparently, this betrayal was only part of a larger plan.
Anima wanted Perfect World.

For reasons still unclear, they sought full control of the layered VR domain. Cornelio remembered the fragments of intelligence they had pieced together... abducted humans, missing recruits, and mind reprogramming to turn humans into slaves.
In any case, the A.I. could not connect to Perfect World directly. Despite their mastery of technology, they lacked something essential... something only humans possessed.
Cornelio sighed as he was sure that the Elders were happy that he had found the evidence they needed. He had already submitted his full report after all.
’In the end... The Anima also needs us. They need our brains... or perhaps our souls.’
He had seen evidence... pods left behind after raids, empty shells where humans had once been.
The victims were not dead, but their consciousness had been hijacked.
Essentially becoming puppets of Anima, forced into Perfect World to act as proxies. It was chilling, and it explained why Anima fought so desperately to control the pods.
Whom~
Suddenly, the hall doors opened, pulling Cornelio from his thoughts.
Kai stepped forward, followed closely by Mei and Farrah. Their eyes still carried the faint excitement of someone who had just logged out of the VR world.
They looked tired but satisfied...
Kai smiled faintly as he recognized the man waiting outside the VR Hall.
"It’s been a while, Sir Cornelio."

After confirming the ores they submitted, they already received their reward from Bart and had been checked by the medic. After that, they were informed that Cornelio was waiting outside, so they weren’t surprised.

Cornelio’s gaze swept over them. He had expected Kai to be alone when he invited him to visit this place. However, there were actually two others who managed to reach the required level in such a short amount of time.
"You Foreign Survivors are cheaters... You leveled up so fast."
Mei and Farrah exchanged glances, unsure how to respond. Kai stepped forward.
"Ahem... We’re special, I guess. And I have three more companions exploring the city. All Level 30 as well."
Cornelio’s eyes widened, then lit up with excitement. "Six of you are at least Level 30..."
"If you reach Level 40 and are assigned a Zodiac, I’ll make sure it’s Aries. We need young blood in our faction..."
Kai, Mei, and Farrah were stunned after hearing this information.
"We need to be assigned to a Zodiac after reaching level 40? Uhmm... That’s nothing to do with our birthdate or something?" Kai asked.
It was certainly a valid question, but Cornelio shook his head.
"Yes... Your birth date doesn’t matter. Anyway, Level 40 is still a long way to go. Don’t think too much of it."
The three could only nod at this new information.

In Cornelio’s mind, he wouldn’t let Kai’s people go to another faction. Especially with Taurus, Capricorn, and Cancer. But for now, he decided not to overwhelm them and just focus on what was in front.
"Tell me. How was the VR World?" Cornelio asked.
Kai’s expression brightened. "It felt real. Even better than reality in some ways. We even gained Strength and Dexterity bonus stats, even though we stayed at Level 1 inside."
Cornelio’s smile lingered as he studied the three.
"Alright... You must be tired. Come, eat with me. The faction’s dining hall is just down the corridor."
Kai, Mei, and Farrah exchanged glances. They weren’t starving, they had eaten well outside the city, but they were curious about the food they had here.
Just like that, they followed Cornelio into a spacious hall where long.
The aroma alone was enough to make them pause.
Platters of roasted meat were laid out, seasoned with herbs Kai didn’t recognize.
Bowls of steaming rice, fragrant stews, and freshly baked bread filled the tables.
"Wow..." Kai could only mutter since his Food Gift Pack couldn’t produce anything close to this.
’I hope my higher grade Gift Packs can provide meat like this.’He mused.
There were even delicate dishes of fruit, sliced and arranged like art. The faction’s cooks clearly weren’t ordinary, this was like food prepared by royal chefs.
Mei tasted a spoonful of stew and nodded. "This... is incredible."
Farrah agreed as she chewed slowly. "Better than anything we’ve had outside."
Kai smiled faintly. "You spoil your guests, Sir Cornelio."
Cornelio chuckled...
As they ate, Cornelio shifted the topic...
"Do you know why I gave you that invitation token, Kai?"
Kai and the three paused as they waited.

"It wasn’t just generosity. Aries needs influence. Whether you join us or not, being friends with strong survivors outside Cameron City is valuable. There are resources we cannot find here, so allies matter."
Kai appreciated the honesty. "I like that you’re straightforward."

Cornelio nodded. "Then let me be even clearer. Perfect World is more than an entertainment and training space... It’s a domain Anima cannot enter. That makes it priceless. Inside, you can gather information, resources, and even skills."

Kai agreed. "Then we should invest in it. I’ll share this information with my team. But tell me... can I purchase the Skill Crystal that leads to Hardened Spirit? And do you have support for Skill Fusion?"
Cornelio raised a brow, amused. "Strong Spirit? Of course, we have it. But what can you give me in return? Energy Cores aren’t what we lack right now."
At this point, Mei and Farrah could guess what Kai could offer.
Soon, he reached into his pack and placed two items on the table... a Gene Stimulant Injector and a Spirit‐boosting potion flask.

chapters.title: Chapter 264: The Trade, The Shop, and The Gamble
paragraphs: Cornelio’s eyes lit up as he saw the two items...
He may not possess an Appraisal Skill that could help him determine the things Kai had taken out, he was already familiar with so many serums, tonics, and pills.
He carefully studied the two items on the table.
"Interesting..." Cornelio muttered as he realized that the stimulant had a similarity with a toned-down version of some Gene Enhancements he had seen before.
Meanwhile, he smelled the rich scent of the Spirit‐Boosting potion flask, and they were similar to Spirit Recovery Pills.
"These aren’t ordinary supplies," Cornelio said slowly.

"If I’m not mistaken, both of these items aren’t something an ordinary physician or alchemist could make. The injector can accelerate gene adaptation or perhaps improve your Gene Skills... and the potion probably restores Spirit Energy faster than most tonics. You know exactly what you’re offering."

Kai nodded calmly. "I do. That’s why I’m asking for that Gene Skill Crystal... If my people in the shelters can obtain it, their Spirit Points will rise. They’ll be able to use their Gene Skills longer and recover faster."
’I have three shelters now... I need more people to have this specific skill set.’Kai thought.
Cornelio tapped the table, considering. "You’re asking for a lot of crystals, then..."
"Yes," Kai admitted.
"I need enough to distribute. At least ten crystals to start. More if possible."
Cornelio exhaled as he considered...
Although he wasn’t the Faction Leader, he could still make such a decision as a Level 80 Survivor.

"Ten Strong Spirit Skill Crystals... that’s certainly possible. But you should know that each one is worth six months of service or fifty B‐Grade Cores. Even with your items, the elders won’t part with them lightly. How many can you provide?"

Kai smiled, "The injector and potion flask... I can supply more of them. Mhmm... My shelters can produce these steadily. If Aries agrees, I’ll provide three of each for one Skill Crystal... Furthermore, I will add one of these items as well."
As Kai said this, he opened his backpack and took out one of the items... The small device called the Atmospheric Water Generator!
Kai immediately explained how it worked, and as soon as Cornelio learned this, he stood up!
After being outside doing various missions to weaken the forces of the A.I. Army, he had seen numerous shelters lacking food and water.
It was one of the common tactics of Anima, after all. By destroying the survivors’ sources of food and water, they’d be able to weaken humans and hunt them down more efficiently.
However, if the shelters possess this device, they’d no longer worry about water!
"Y-you can create more of these?" Cornelio asked in excitement.
’Nice reaction...’Kai smiled as he knew that the man was hooked. It was time to negotiate...
Just like that, in just an hour, the two sealed their agreement.
Cornelio was also satisfied.

"Then it’s settled. One Atmospheric Water Generator for one Skill Fusion Crystal. And three Gene Stimulant Injectors plus three Spirit‐Boosting Potions for either one Strong Spirit Skill Crystal or one Palm Shock Skill Crystal."
Kai nodded firmly. He was pleased with the arrangement.
Strong Spirit was essential for the Survivors in his Shelters... It also gave them a chance to create the Hardened Spirit Gene Skill.
As for the Palm Shock, it opened the path toward Stonebreaker Impact... a devastating skill that could change the tide in combat. Both were valuable, and now he had a way to secure them.
Still, a concern lingered in his mind.
His Water Gift Packs produced other items. They were useful, but not always needed. He couldn’t reveal this detail to Cornelio, but he needed a solution.

Kai cleared his throat. "Sir Cornelio, I have another request. I’ll need storage space. A warehouse, or something similar. I plan to open a small shop here in Cameron City to manage surplus items and trade them properly."
Cornelio gently nodded as he knew that Kai realized the value of having a property in this city.
"A shop, huh? You think ahead, Kai. That’s good. We encourage enterprise within Aries."
He then considered what he should do about it and recalled the people who could help.

"I’ll speak with Officer Jess, the one in charge of our Commerce and Logistics Office. That department handles all faction businesses... warehousing, trade permits, shop rentals, and the regulation of goods moving in and out of Cameron City. Permission won’t be a problem once I vouch for you. As for the price, that will be negotiated later in his office."
"That sounds perfect..." Kai muttered.
"Of course... If you’re serious about opening a shop, Aries will make space for you... It’ll be better for our reputation." Cornelio admitted.
Kai’s lips curved into a faint smile. "That’s all I ask. A place to store and trade..."
It didn’t take that long before Kai, Mei, and Farrah left the Aries compound with quiet satisfaction.
Soon, they returned to the Silver Rest Inn.
Inside, the siblings were already gathered around a table with Claire, Ralph, and Alfie, enjoying a simple meal.
"Hey... You didn’t wait for us." Kai said as he joined in.

After a few laughs, he no longer wasted time as he shared their experience. He explained how the VR World felt almost real, how mining mystic iron ore had given them stat bonuses, and how Cornelio had revealed the deeper secrets of Perfect World.

Most importantly, he told them about the deal he had struck... trading hisrareitems for Skill Crystals, securing Strong Spirit and Palm Shock, and arranging to rent a warehouse and open a shop in Cameron City.
The others listened in amazement, impressed by the opportunity Kai had carved out for their group.

Claire clasped her hands... "That’s incredible. After going around for some time, we learned that getting a permit or a stall here isn’t going to be easy. Having a connection in this place is really much better."
Then, Ralph and Alfie exchanged glances before sharing what they had discovered around town. "There’s something else you should know," Ralph began.
"Gambling is huge here. Not dice or cards... but blood duels."

He then considered what he should do about it and recalled the people who could help.
"I’ll speak with Officer Jess, the one in charge of our Commerce and Logistics Office.
That department handles all faction businesses... warehousing, trade permits, shop rentals, and the regulation of goods moving in and out of Cameron City.
Permission won’t be a problem once I vouch for you.
As for the price, that will be negotiated later in his office."
"That sounds perfect..." Kai muttered.
"Of course...
If you’re serious about opening a shop, Aries will make space for you...
It’ll be better for our reputation." Cornelio admitted.
Kai’s lips curved into a faint smile.
"That’s all I ask.
A place to store and trade..."
It didn’t take that long before Kai, Mei, and Farrah left the Aries compound with quiet satisfaction.
Soon, they returned to the Silver Rest Inn.
Inside, the siblings were already gathered around a table with Claire, Ralph, and Alfie, enjoying a simple meal.
"Hey...
You didn’t wait for us." Kai said as he joined in.
After a few laughs, he no longer wasted time as he shared their experience.
He explained how the VR World felt almost real, how mining mystic iron ore had given them stat bonuses, and how Cornelio had revealed the deeper secrets of Perfect World.

Most importantly, he told them about the deal he had struck... trading hisrareitems for Skill Crystals, securing Strong Spirit and Palm Shock, and arranging to rent a warehouse and open a shop in Cameron City.
The others listened in amazement, impressed by the opportunity Kai had carved out for their group.
Claire clasped her hands...
"That’s incredible.
After going around for some time, we learned that getting a permit or a stall here isn’t going to be easy.
Having a connection in this place is really much better."
Then, Ralph and Alfie exchanged glances before sharing what they had discovered around town.
"There’s something else you should know," Ralph began.
"Gambling is huge here.
Not dice or cards... but blood duels."

chapters.title: Chapter 265: The Duels and the Shop!
paragraphs: Kai’s expression darkened as Ralph shared the news.
"What blood duels?" he repeated... "Wait... You mean survivors fight each other to death... for gambling?"
Mei’s eyes widened. "That’s insane. People risk their lives just so others can place bets? Why is it happening here? Aren’t they supposed to work together to fight against the A.I. Army?"
Farrah shook her head slowly, unease written across her face.
"It explains the crowds we saw earlier. I thought it was just another market gathering... but if duels are drawing people in, then Cameron City thrives on more than trade."

Alfie chuckled as he could understand what they were feeling now. Then, he smiled despite the grim subject. "You should’ve seen it. Survivors clashing with Gene Skills, the crowd was cheering like it was a festival. You’re all probably inside the VR World when the battle was happening. Anyway, some fighters were throwing fire after putting oil in their mouth, others were using shockwaves or blades enhanced by their genes."
Alfie continued sharing what he saw in the duels. Then, Mei got curious and asked if the fighters were getting something from the duel.

"Yes... Organizers hand out rewards. It’s mostly money, but if they perform well, they can get a space where they can live permanently within the city. After all, most of the fighters were outsiders with only temporary residence."
"Ohhh... So that’s why they’re willing to participate even with the possibility of death." Farrah nodded.
"Also... if they really performed well, they may be recruited by the factions around the city. Still, the real money comes from the wagers. It’s brutal, but profitable."
Claire added...

"And it’s everywhere. Taverns, squares, even small arenas. The city treats it like entertainment. Some fighters looked desperate, clearly gambling their lives for food. Others were more polished or disciplined... almost professional, like they’d trained for this. Either way, the crowd didn’t care... they just wanted blood."

Ralph nodded. "We even heard jokes that a skilled fighter could earn more in a week of duels than in months of missions. Food, Energy Cores, and even rare items are wagered. It’s dangerous, but tempting."
Kai couldn’t help but feel curious.
After all, he might even join the battle if he found a reward that was worth enough...

"It’s tempting... But it’s also a trap. Once you step into that arena, you’re marked. People will remember your face, your skills. And not all attention is good. Anyway, is there a duel between robots? You know... like Atom."
Claire and the other two paused as they tried to recall if they had seen one but soon, they shook their heads.
"I’ve never seen one. Perhaps we haven’t explored... Who knows... We might fight one if we search further north of the city."
"Well... It’s ok." Kai replied with a chuckle. He wasn’t really being serious. After all, even if there was, he wouldn’t risk Atom... unless he was 100% confident that an A-Grade Unit could win.
Mei frowned, glancing at Kai. "Are you thinking of joining? It’s not like you’re short in supplies..."
"Haha! That’s true. I’ll keep it in mind."
Farrah sighed. "It’s a city of spectacle. VR World, Factions, and now blood duels. Everything here is about risk and reward."
Alfie smirked. "Well, if we ever run low, we could always bet on ourselves. Imagine the look on their faces when outsiders sweep the arena."
As someone with a Gladiator Talent, he was confident that he’d dominate a battle if they were all at similar levels.
The group laughed, easing the tension for a moment.
Yet beneath the humor, the reality was clear...
Cameron City’s duels weren’t just games. They were dangerous paths, offering fortune or ruin.
In any case, Alfie just continued sharing...

"We also saw exosuit matches, too. No Active Gene Skills allowed... just raw strength and tactics with your machine. Survivors strapped into heavy suits, slamming into each other like machines. It was quite entertaining to watch. The crowd loved it because it felt fair. No hidden powers, just steel against steel."
"Fair? I don’t think so. The one with better ironworks and engineers wins." Claire muttered.
Kai couldn’t help but frown after hearing this.
"Exosuits... That’s right, Claire. This type of battle means survivors with resources can dominate. Those suits aren’t cheap."
They had all seen the Iron Phalanx before and how they fought against the Beast Class units of the A.I. Army.
Those machines weren’t cheap to make... Anyone who participates in such gambling or duels must also prepare for the repair costs of these machines, and that wouldn’t be cheap.
Mei muttered, "So there are tiers of gambling. Blood duels for the desperate, exosuit matches for the well‐equipped... What? Is there also gambling on Perfect World’s duels or something?"
"That wouldn’t be surprising anymore, to be honest." Kai muttered.
Farrah shook her head as she believed that the duel in the Perfect World didn’t really matter that much.
"Ahem... It’s dangerous, but it’s also an opportunity. I think that with my Skill, I can actually win a few fights." She muttered.
Kai shook his head. "You just barely passed Level 30... You will have difficulty fighting against those Level 40 and above."
Alfie chuckled. "Oh. There’s actually a rule about that. Don’t worry. I’m actually thinking of participating in tomorrow’s event.
Claire smiled as she looked at Alfie. The two of them have already discussed this.
"What?" Kai frowned.
"Yes... Don’t worry. It’s restricted to survivors Level 39 and below. The prize isn’t just money or food... it’s a full exosuit."
The table went silent.
"A full exosuit?" Farrah repeated.
Mei and Kai nodded as they heard this...
"No wonder people risk their lives. An exosuit could change everything for a shelter. It’s protection, firepower, and status all in one."
He had seen the exosuits of the Iron Phalanx before and witnessed how exosuits turned battles against the A.I. Army. Owning one wasn’t just about strength... it was about survival.
"That’s worth the risk," Kai muttered.
Alfie laughed... "Haha.. That’s right. I knew you’d see it that way. Tomorrow’s duel will be brutal, if you join, Kai."
Just like that, Kai made a firm decision.
However, the next day, a messenger from the Aries Faction arrived, confirming that a store building and warehouse had been rented to him at a dirt-cheap price.

chapters.title: Chapter 266: The Store and the Products
paragraphs: The messenger had a higher level than Kai and the others.
However, since he was under Cornelio’s orders, he bowed slightly after handing over the keys. He didn’t show any haughtiness or signs that he was looking down on them.
He even spoke respectfully.
"If you’d like, Sir Kai, I can guide you there now. The Commerce District isn’t far, but it’s easy to get lost among the stalls and warehouses."
Kai glanced at Mei, Farrah, Alfie, Claire, Ralph, and the siblings Xian and Xinyi.
He nodded. "We’ll all go. Better to see it together."
The group set out, following the messenger through Cameron City’s bustling streets.
Xian and Xinyi also walked close to each other. They were still thin from their hardships, but no longer frail like before.
After receiving Gene Enhancement Serums from Kai and eating proper meals for a couple of days, their faces had regained color.
Furthermore, they were able to endure consuming at least 10 drops each before sensing that they could no longer improve, which was already quite amazing.
It appears that they needed another month or so to fully absorb the Gene Enhancements before being allowed to consume more.
Xinyi flexed her new arm as they walked. There was a faint smile tugging at her lips as she fixed her blue hair...
She then whispered to her brother, "I feel like I could smash a house without a problem."
Xian chuckled nervously after hearing this, but there was pride in his eyes.
"Just don’t break any more glasses. I don’t know how to apologize to them any longer."
"Y-yeah... I promise that won’t happen again."
Soon, the messenger led them into the Commerce District.
The atmosphere shifted immediately. It was less chaotic than the outer markets and it was more structured.
Rows of shops lined the streets, each marked with banners and signs, while warehouses stood behind them...
Merchants here weren’t shouting prices, but they were actively enticing customers to buy from them by doing demos, giving samples, giving rewards, and others.
Of course, aside from the buyers around, there were also carts loaded with goods that rattled across the cobblestones.
Finally, they stopped before a modest two‐story building.
The shopfront wasn’t grand, but it looked sturdy and was being taken care of... It had shutters and a wide counter space inside.
The warehouse connected to the back was also larger than Kai expected. It had iron‐bound doors and enough room to store crates, barrels, and supplies for several shelters.
"This is yours now," the messenger said proudly.

"The Aries Faction has approved it. Fifty C‐Grade Energy Cores per month, fixed. You’ll find no better deal in this district. It also means that if you reach Level 40, you have to consider the Aries Zodiac first before anything else..."
"I understand." Kai nodded.
It was still up to him whether to choose Aries and bear its last name. He liked how they weren’t forcing him, so he would view them positively.
Kai then stepped inside, running his hand along the counter.
The place was not dusty as he thought it would, but there was a smell of old wood.
Still, just a bit of cleaning would be more than enough.
He imagined shelves lined with stimulants, potions, and devices from his Infinite Gift Packs or even weapons.
He pictured survivors crowding the shop, desperate for items they couldn’t find anywhere else but here...
Mei then walked through the warehouse and knew that Kai would make full use of this.
After all, she was already pretty much aware of how Kai’s Talent worked.
"It’s bigger than I thought. We could store everything here... food packs, medical kits, even some entertainment materials."
Farrah also tapped the iron door. "Strong enough to keep thieves out. This is good."
Alfie grinned. "Imagine the faces of the merchants when they see what you’ll be selling. I’m sure you’ll be flooding the market with rare items."
Kai’s lips curved into a faint smile. He knew Alfie was right.
His Infinite Gift Packs would disrupt the balance of trade in Cameron City. Merchants would probably complain, factions might take notice, and prices would shift.
But Kai didn’t care.
He needed Energy Cores, Skill Crystals, and rare materials. He needed everything that could strengthen his shelters and prepare them for the war against Anima.
"We just need enough strength to protect ourselves." Kai muttered.
"We’ll sell what we have. If the market shakes, so be it. I need cores, and I need items. That’s all that matters..."
Xinyi, still flexing her new arm, laughed softly. "You sound so cool, Brother Kai... Please hire me as a cleaner! I’m good at cleaning!"
She then held Xian’s arm and continued. "We’ll work really hard!"
"Haha... Of course, you can help around. You can live here for a while." Kai chuckled as he shuffled the young girl’s hair.
Xian also felt excited. He was also determined to work here. He noticed that there were staff rooms that they could use to live here, and he wouldn’t pass up the opportunity.
"Brother Kai... thank you. You’ve given us more than we ever dreamed."

Kai nodded. Initially, he wanted to bring Xian to New Haven-45 to maximize his Title Effect. However, he realized that they were still children, and they weren’t that desperate to make Xian and Xinyi their combatants.
They might as well safely grow in this city, where no A.I. Army could breach.
Kai looked around the shop once again, and soon, it was decided that Mei, Claire, and Ralph would stay here with the siblings to clean the place, so they could soon open their shop...
Then, Kai went to the warehouse and unloaded several Gift Packs...
"Let’s fill a small part of this warehouse," Kai muttered as he opened his Talent System.
After some time, he unloaded a total of 30 Superior Water Gift Packs, 30 Superior Survival Tools Gift Packs, and 30 Superior Transport Gift Packs.
After that, Kai went to another corner, and this time, he opened his Enhanced Gift Packs. Then, he selected 50 Food Gift Packs and 50 Shelter Gift Packs from them...
"Alright... I’ll leave these things to you to organize." Kai said as he looked at this work.
"We’re going to check the Blood Duel..." Kai said as he ignored the stunned faces of Xian and Xinyi...
The two of them heard that Foreign Survivors had a mystical Inventory System, but they didn’t expect that they could hold this many resources!

chapters.title: Chapter 268: The Shop
paragraphs: As soon as the crowd heard about the Death Gaze, everyone felt excited, tempted to go down and challenge Rufus immediately!

Death Gaze was infamous... It was a Gene Skill that could paralyze or kill with a single look. Well, it was not useful against the A.I. Army, but against mutants or humans you couldn’t reason with, it was a perfect skill.
Kai and the other two just listened to the conversation of the crowd, and they already learned what kind of Gene Skill it was.
Needless to say, they were also tempted.
However, as the announcer’s loud voice echoed across the arena, three figures stepped forward from the crowd.
Each of them looked determined with their eyes fixed on Rufus.
The announcer raised his hand, acknowledging them.
"Ah, brave challengers! Three survivors willing to test their strength against Rufus!" The crowd erupted in cheers...
But then the announcer’s tone shifted, and he sounded more formal this time.

"Though you have declared your intent, the duel will not happen today. You must first register and pay the challenge fee. Tomorrow, you will face Rufus in the arena. Should Rufus fall before your turn, your fee will be refunded in full."
The three nodded, stepping aside to meet with officials at the registration booth.
Meanwhile, Rufus, drenched in sweat and visibly exhausted, finally lowered his sword. He gave the crowd one last glance before leaving the arena...
"Looks like that’s it for today, huh..." Kai muttered.
Alfie shrugged. "Not bad. At least we saw Rufus fight. Tomorrow will be even crazier."
But just as they turned to leave, the announcer’s voice thundered once more, stopping them in their tracks.
"Attention! Attention! For all survivors Level 39 and below... today you too can fight! Registration is open now for only ten C‐Grade Energy Cores!"
The crowd stirred as they knew that this announcement wasn’t done yet.

The announcer grinned, and as expected, he continued. "The reward may not be as legendary as Death Gaze, but it is still precious! Today’s prize is a Life Pill... granting permanent vitality, a boost to your health points!"
The crowd was impressed once again.
Kai gently nodded...
’A Life Pill... permanent vitality. That’s no ordinary prize. Even if it’s not Death Gaze, it’s still worth fighting for.
Farrah’s lips parted slightly. "Permanent vitality boost? That’s... incredible. Survivors would kill for that."
As expected, many people decided to register...
Well, the Life Pill was tempting... permanent vitality was no small prize. For a moment, all three considered stepping forward.
But then the first batch of registrants appeared.
The crowd parted as several survivors walked toward the booth.

Their appearances were unsettling... There were mutations and augmentations that made them look less human and more monstrous. One had four eyes that glowed faintly, and another had three eyes stacked vertically across his forehead. A third had a tail swaying behind him, while yet another had an extra arm protruding from his side.
Some even had huge mouths to the point that they could probably eat a whole coconut nut.
Farrah’s face paled. "They look... terrifying."
Kai listened to the whispers around them.
"Cancer Faction rejects," someone muttered.
"Or maybe remnants of their experiments."
Kai was shocked.
’So even the Cancer Faction’s failures find their way here. And they’re desperate enough to fight for scraps.’

Alfie whistled low. "These aren’t ordinary fighters."

’Even if we joined, the risk is too high. These people aren’t just normal survivors... they’re living weapons.’

"Nope... Let’s not. We’ll gain more by selling in your store, Kai. We don’t need to throw ourselves into this madness."
Kai laughed at this since she was right.
"Agreed. Those rewards aren’t for us..."
Though they had felt confident earlier because of their Gene Skills and various enhancements, they realized after seeing those mutated humans that they were still not at that level.
They weren’t survivors willing to abandon their humanity just yet, unlike these newly arrived people.
They couldn’t imagine wishing for multiple eyes or limbs like them.
Alfie also sighed...
"Fine. I’ll admit, I wanted to test myself... but you’re right. This isn’t the time."

Hassan’s gaze shifted again, and he nearly stopped in his tracks. They were actually selling a portable drone scout!.
As he walked deeper into the shop, he realized there was far more here than he had expected!
"W-what is this store?!"

chapters.title: Chapter 269: The Return and The Stalker
paragraphs: Hassan was shocked. Near the counter, his eyes landed on something that was definitely rare within the city... an off‐road motorbike that ran on diesel.
"Ugh... you’re selling one of these?" Hassan asked, his voice filled with disbelief.
Although diesel was hard to come by, since Energy Cores from the A.I. Army were already the standard fuel, it wasn’t impossible to obtain from certain traders.
The shopkeeper, a beautiful woman with short black hair standing behind the counter, smiled faintly.
"Yes. We have more of them at the back. This one is just a display. Do you want to test one?"
Hassan blinked, stunned.
He had seen many shops in Cameron City, but none like this.
’Kai’s Survival Store wasn’t just another merchant’s stall... it was a treasure trove.’
"Ahem... Let me look around first, Miss... Mei." Hassan said as he saw Mei’s nameplate.

Mei then gestured for him to continue exploring the shop. Everyone was like this anyway. They were all curious about this new shop, and soon, they’d spend all their hard-earned Energy Cores, Gene Enhancement Serums, and other valuables on them.
"This is incredible..."
Hassan muttered as he continued walking through the aisles.

On one side, he noticed vacuum‐sealed rations stacked neatly beside canned goods, dried fruits, and nuts. There were even coffee sachets and portable cooking stoves with fuel canisters... luxuries that most survivors outside could only dream of.
Further down, he spotted field tents, insulated sleeping bags, and thermal blankets, all arranged in perfect order.
He reached out to touch a heavy‐duty raincoat, feeling the thick, durable fabric between his fingers. "This... this could last through any storm," he muttered.
He was impressed with its quality!
Before he could examine it further, the door opened, and another customer entered, followed by two attendants.
The man in front looked rugged, clearly a survivor who had seen his share of battles. Without hesitation, he walked straight to the shelf Hassan had just been inspecting.
"I’ll take all of these," the man said firmly, pointing at the stack of heavy‐duty raincoats.
Hassan’s eyes widened.
It seemed that this was a returning customer.
Still, the shopkeeper wasn’t surprised as she nodded calmly. It was as if bulk purchases were nothing unusual here.
"Of course. We’ll prepare them for you. Please wait a moment."
The man handed over a pouch filled with Energy Cores... the faint glow of their power illuminating his scarred hands.
Hassan watched in disbelief as the transaction was completed smoothly, the shopkeeper moved efficiently, and soon, the raincoats on display were refilled by a new batch by the other workers.
’I wonder who’s the owner of this store. What faction is it? Or maybe this is a multi-faction company?’
Since there were so many unusual items here that couldn’t be found elsewhere, he could only guess that much.
In the end, he looked at the beautiful shopkeeper and spoke.
"Ahem... Can I do a test drive, Miss Mei?"
After a week within the city, Kai had already decided to leave the safety of Cameron City.
The reason was obvious... he had to level up.
Remaining inside the city walls would only hinder his growth.
After walking about five kilometers away from the city, Kai noticed that he was being followed.
However, he didn’t care at this point.
He opened his inventory and summoned his Modified Dragoon.
Sliding into the driver’s seat, he activated the system.
With a low hum, the vehicle lifted off the ground, hovering like a jet ski that could soar through the sky!
"Catch me if you can..." Kai said as he guessed that the person following him was ordered by Humphrey from the Cancer Faction.
Whoosh~
The wind rushed past him as he accelerated, leaving the city behind.
His companions remained in Cameron City to operate the store under the protection of the Aries Faction.
Kai had made sure they had enough supplies before departing.
For now, his path led toward the Blue Grass Shelter.
Kai smiled faintly as he thought about how far his influence had spread.
His Codebreakers Guild was slowly becoming a force to be reckoned with.
Aside from the small store within the city, he had already secured New Haven‐45 and Freedom Shelter, both once A.I. bases.
Then there was Haven‐28, previously owned by Angelo until Kai eliminated him and his lackeys.
And lastly, the Blue Grass Shelter. It was practically under his control ever since Vera and the others had been saved by his Atmospheric Water Generator.
In return for being invited to his Guild, they had promised to provide him with Soul‐Booster Potions, a resource that would strengthen his forces even further.
But as he traveled for a couple of days and got closer to the shelter, Kai’s smile faded.
Smoke rose in the distance, and he realized what was going on...
The Blue Grass Shelter was under attack.
From above, he counted at least ten Sentinels!
Their metallic frames were undeniable...
Each was equipped with swords and guns, moving in coordinated patterns as they pressed against the defenders.
Kai’s first instinct was to intervene.
His hand tightened on the controls, ready to unleash his arsenal.
But then he paused and watched the situation carefully...
The defenders of the shelter weren’t panicking. Instead, they moved without hesitation as they wielded weapons that Kai recognized immediately.
They were compact grappling launchers... the very ones he had distributed from his Gift Packs.
With practiced skill, the defenders fired the launchers, entangling the Sentinels in thick cords. The machines failed to move as they wanted due to the restriction!
With that move alone, the Sentinels’ balanced where destroyed!
In that moment of vulnerability, the survivors used a smokescreen for cover and struck the Sentinels with blunt weapons to crush their circuits!
Kai hovered above, impressed by their method of attack...
’Nice...They’re using the tools I gave them to fight back.
The Sentinel tried to fight back... However, they were too slow because of the wires around them!
A defender rolled aside, firing another grappling hook that wrapped around its legs.
The machine toppled, crashing into the dirt!
Thud!
Within seconds, three survivors swarmed it, stabbing and shooting until it lay still.
The battle was brutal, but it was clear the shelter had adapted!
"Good job..." Kai muttered as he knew that it was already done.
However, he soon turned back after realizing that they had visitors...
"Seriously... You followed me up to here?"

chapters.title: Chapter 270: Spy Elimination
paragraphs: Kai had learned from Cornelio Aries that the members of the Cancer Faction were a bit too extreme in their ways.
However, because of their great contribution in battles against the A.I. Army, no one would really dare to reprimand them.

If they’re gone or have decided not to help the frontline battles, a handful of Level 80 Survivors would stop showing up in battles against the Ascendant Units of Anima... and that would be a true disaster.

After all, the only reason the city was able to avoid being invaded was because of the Survivors’ ability to fend off these Ascendant Units... and of course, the barrier they were maintaining that could stop the Energy Beams of the alien forces.
"Hey... Are you from Cameron? Why are you following me? I don’t have money with me." Kai said as he provoked the five people who were using Stealth Abilities.
The five were surprised as soon as they realized that they had failed in their ambush.
"How?" One of them muttered as he cancelled his stealth mode.
However, Kai just smiled. He didn’t want to reveal his secrets.
In truth, he was able to notice them despite being far from the range of his Keen Sense, thanks to a simple item from his Superior Grade Stealth Gift Pack... the thermal detection goggles.
"Are you going to attack now? Or are you running away?" Kai asked in a mocking tone.
The five figures no longer responded to Kai’s provocation.
Instead, they broke into motion, their silhouettes started appearing as all their Stealth Abilities dropped.
Kai smiled as he saw them...

From their speed alone, he could tell they were higher level than him... probably around Level 40. But fear never crossed his mind. He was floating above them on his Modified Dragoon, while they were stuck on the ground.
Their only options were throwing weapons or gunfire, and Kai had prepared for this exact scenario.
Bang! Bang! Bang!
Soon, the assassins raised their rifles, firing upward in synchronized bursts.
Whoosh~ Whoosh~
Bullets streaked through the air, but the elevated angle worked against them. The rounds pinged harmlessly off the Dragoon’s reinforced plating!
’Victor really did well... This is such a solid modification.’
Kai smirked.
Then he decided to end this as quickly as possible.
"Pathetic Assassins. Stay there!"
Kai didn’t wait for the reply as he moved the grenade launcher into position.
With a loudthunk, the first round launched downward, exploding in a concussive blast that sent two assassins sprawling.
Boom!
Dust and smoke filled the battlefield, forcing them to scatter.
Without hesitation, Kai switched to his semi‐automatic pistol. His shots were precise with this weapon as each bullet forced the assassins to dive for cover.
He wasn’t aiming to kill outright... he was suppressing them, keeping them pinned while the Dragoon hovered steadily above.

The assassins tried to regroup, firing again, but their bullets barely scratched the Dragoon’s armor. Kai’s elevated position gave him complete control of the fight. With the Grenade Launcher, they couldn’t find a perfect spot!
Then, a shadow fell across the battlefield.
A metallic figure landed with a heavythud.
"Ohhh! You’re finally here! Perfect! Protect me please!" Kai shouted.
Needless to say, the one who had just arrived was Atom. His only A‐Grade Sentinel had arrived.
The assassins froze, their eyes widening in shock. They had expected to fight a human survivor, not an android.
"An android?! He has a Sentinel?!" one of them shouted, and soon panic broke through their discipline.
They immediately tried to adjust, switching weapons to armor‐piercing rounds. But it was too late.
Atom moved with terrifying speed, his blade was already on their chests!
The first assassin raised his gun, but Atom’s arm shot forward, crushing the weapon before driving a fist into the man’s chest.
Bang!
The impact sent him flying.
Another assassin threw a blade, but Atom deflected it effortlessly, then countered with a sweeping strike that tore through two enemies at once.
Gunfire erupted, but Atom’s reinforced plating absorbed the rounds.
The assassins had prepared for human targets, not machines. Their weapons were insufficient, their tactics useless.
Kai watched from above, his pistol still aimed at the battlefield. "You should’ve stayed in Cameron."
Atom tore through the remaining assassins quite easily...
One tried to retreat, but Atom’s grappling line shot out, yanking him back before a crushing blow silenced him.
Bang!
Another attempted to flank, only to be caught mid‐step and dismantled by Atom.
Within moments, the battlefield was silent. The five assassins lay broken with their weapons scattered across the dirt.
Kai lowered his Dragoon, landing beside Atom.
He glanced at the wreckage, then at the Sentinel standing tall beside him.
"They thought they could ambush me," Kai muttered. "But they weren’t prepared for you."
Atom’s optics glowed faintly, scanning the area for any remaining threats. But none remained.
Kai holstered his pistol, his expression calm. "Humphrey really wants me gone, huh? Sending high-level assassins... and still failing."
He then looked toward the hill where smoke from the Blue Grass Shelter still rose.
"No time to waste. Let’s move."
Meanwhile, as Kai was busy at the Blue Grass Shelter, a visitor arrived at New Haven‐45.
And it wasn’t just anyone... it was Renji, one of the most renowned survivors, always ranked within the Top 10 of the Survivors Leaderboard.
Unsurprisingly, Renji came in peace. According to his story, he had been traveling alone for more than two weeks, and exhaustion clung to him heavily.
All he wanted now was a safe place to rest, even if only for a couple of days. He was willing to pay for 1 C-Grade Cores per night.
Because he sounded generous, he was welcomed by Marissa and Victor.
Victor, ever cautious, studied Renji’s movements carefully. His hand lingered near the hilt of his weapon, ready to act if things turned hostile.

Marissa, on the other hand, stood calm but alert. As a Witch Doctor, she carried a hidden advantage... if Renji revealed bad intentions, she could curse him instantly, crippling his strength before he even realized what had happened.
Renji, of course, had no idea of this hidden safeguard... He couldn’t even take his eyes off her!
"Miss... Do you want to get stronger? I can help you get even stronger... Here, look at this." Renji muttered while showing an unfamiliar Gene Enhancement Serum...
"This isn’t from a Gene Trader you’re familiar with but from someone within Anima’s Territory. What do you think?"

They had expected to fight a human survivor, not an android.
"An android?!
He has a Sentinel?!" one of them shouted, and soon panic broke through their discipline.
They immediately tried to adjust, switching weapons to armor‐piercing rounds.
But it was too late.
Atom moved with terrifying speed, his blade was already on their chests!
The first assassin raised his gun, but Atom’s arm shot forward, crushing the weapon before driving a fist into the man’s chest.
Bang!
The impact sent him flying.
Another assassin threw a blade, but Atom deflected it effortlessly, then countered with a sweeping strike that tore through two enemies at once.
Gunfire erupted, but Atom’s reinforced plating absorbed the rounds.
The assassins had prepared for human targets, not machines.
Their weapons were insufficient, their tactics useless.
Kai watched from above, his pistol still aimed at the battlefield.
"You should’ve stayed in Cameron."
Atom tore through the remaining assassins quite easily...
One tried to retreat, but Atom’s grappling line shot out, yanking him back before a crushing blow silenced him.
Bang!
Another attempted to flank, only to be caught mid‐step and dismantled by Atom.
Within moments, the battlefield was silent.
The five assassins lay broken with their weapons scattered across the dirt.
Kai lowered his Dragoon, landing beside Atom.
He glanced at the wreckage, then at the Sentinel standing tall beside him.
"They thought they could ambush me," Kai muttered.
"But they weren’t prepared for you."
Atom’s optics glowed faintly, scanning the area for any remaining threats.
But none remained.
Kai holstered his pistol, his expression calm.
"Humphrey really wants me gone, huh?
Sending high-level assassins... and still failing."
He then looked toward the hill where smoke from the Blue Grass Shelter still rose.
"No time to waste.
Let’s move."
Meanwhile, as Kai was busy at the Blue Grass Shelter, a visitor arrived at New Haven‐45.
And it wasn’t just anyone... it was Renji, one of the most renowned survivors, always ranked within the Top 10 of the Survivors Leaderboard.
Unsurprisingly, Renji came in peace.
According to his story, he had been traveling alone for more than two weeks, and exhaustion clung to him heavily.
All he wanted now was a safe place to rest, even if only for a couple of days.
He was willing to pay for 1 C-Grade Cores per night.
Because he sounded generous, he was welcomed by Marissa and Victor.
Victor, ever cautious, studied Renji’s movements carefully.
His hand lingered near the hilt of his weapon, ready to act if things turned hostile.
Marissa, on the other hand, stood calm but alert.
As a Witch Doctor, she carried a hidden advantage... if Renji revealed bad intentions, she could curse him instantly, crippling his strength before he even realized what had happened.
Renji, of course, had no idea of this hidden safeguard...
He couldn’t even take his eyes off her!
"Miss...
Do you want to get stronger?
I can help you get even stronger...
Here, look at this." Renji muttered while showing an unfamiliar Gene Enhancement Serum...
"This isn’t from a Gene Trader you’re familiar with but from someone within Anima’s Territory.
What do you think?"

chapters.title: Chapter 271: The Strength of Renji and the Powerful Shelter
paragraphs: In the meantime, while Renji was speaking with Marissa and Victor, there were others secretly observing the situation.
Hidden in the shadows of the shelter’s perimeter were Augustine and Russel, the two scouts assigned to New Haven‐45.
They had been the ones to notice Renji’s approach through the surveillance drones they controlled, and now they watched closely, waiting for any sign of hostility.
Of course, the scouts weren’t alone in their vigilance.
Hidden in rooms and behind the walls were five modified Sentinel units. They were X‐02 through X‐06. stood silently in standby mode.
They were monitoring closely, ready to activate at the first sign of trouble.
If Renji made a suspicious move, the Sentinels would strike without hesitation.
Marissa and Victor, meanwhile, led Renji into the lounge of the main building.

Their intent was clear... they wanted him to touch the Status Crystal. It was the only way to confirm whether he was truly a survivor from Earth or something far more dangerous... an android disguised in human skin.
In these times, caution was survival. The A.I. Army had proven it could infiltrate in terrifying ways, and no one could afford to take chances.
Renji seemed aware of the scrutiny.
His eyes even turned toward the corners of the room, as if he could sense the hidden Sentinels and the scouts watching from above.
Yet he didn’t resist. Instead, he stepped forward and placed his hand on the Status Crystal.
"You want to check me with this, right? Here... Have a look." Renji muttered.
Soon, the crystal pulsed with light, and a blue screen hovered above it, revealing Renji’s details:
Code
[ Name: Renji ]
[ Title: Resourceful Survivor, Lone Wanderer, Mechanic’s Hand ]
[ Level: 31 ]
[ Active Skills: Gearshift Dash Lv5, Mettalic Aura Lv5, Overclock Burst Lv4 ]
[ Passive Skills: Metal Body Lv5, Precision Assembly Lv5, Adaptive Reflexes Lv5 ]
The room fell silent as the information appeared.
Victor couldn’t help but have a double look...
"Level 31... not bad. You’ve been fighting hard out there."
Marissa studied the skills carefully before the information vanished in the air...
’Mechanic’s Hand... movement and engineering‐based abilities. He’s not a typical fighter... I wonder how he survived the field outside.’
Augustine whispered to Russel through the comms. "He’s legit. Not an android. But I wonder why he’s hiding those things from us..."

Russel nodded, though his tone remained cautious. "Maybe he has a reason. Let’s just wait until the reinforcements arrive. He’s still a Top 10 survivor... Showing up here unannounced is never just a coincidence."
Meanwhile, Renji withdrew his hand from the crystal, his expression calm.
"Satisfied?" he asked, his voice carrying a faint edge.
"I told you... I’m just here to rest. Or maybe purchase some resources. I’ve been alone too long. Even someone like me needs a roof sometimes."

Victor didn’t lower his guard, but he stepped back slightly. "Alright... You’ll get your rest. But since you’re here, you follow our rules. Do not go to those restricted rooms and buildings and we won’t have a problem. We’re not that cruel to fellow Survivors. You can even join us permanently if you wanted. You just have to complete a few tasks."
Renji gave a faint smile, though it didn’t reach his eyes. "I’m not planning to join any Guild at the moment. In any case, your rules are fine. I’ve lived by harsher ones."
Soon, Renji was given one of the small wooden houses located at the far end of the eastern wall of the shelter.
Needless to say, the materials used to create these wooden houses were from various Material Treasure Chests that had been opened by several Survivors...
They contained not just various ingots and steel plates for crafting but also rolls of various fabrics and wooden planks!
"Interesting..." Renji muttered as he observed the small house.
No one was surveilling him anymore, as if the people of this shelter believed that his privacy mattered.
After sitting down on his bed, he realized that it was actually quite well-made, and was impressed.
It had been some time since he had this comfort.
"It’s a pity I didn’t get to see the Rank 1 Survivor," Renji muttered while thinking of Kai, the man at the top of the Leaderboard.
"He actually went away, huh... It wouldn’t be surprising if he were brave enough to enter the city."
He knew the dangers within Cameron City. He had solid information that an organization there called Cancer Faction was collecting human survivors to be used in experiments.
If such a vile organization was actually in that place without being reprimanded or raided, he believed that Cameron City wasn’t safe.
Renji soon drifted into sleep, his body finally surrendering to exhaustion.
Just like that, the night passed quietly until his eyes snapped open.
Instinct guided him... he checked his surroundings, confirming that no one was monitoring his room.
Still, patrols moved across the shelter grounds.
It was necessary. The A.I. Army could strike anywhere, anytime, as long as humans are present...
This time, however, Renji knew an attack was inevitable.
"Sorry..." He muttered.
It was not because of foresight, but because he was being followed.
Of course, it was bad manners to lure A.I. soldiers to a peaceful shelter, but he had reached his limit.
His strength was waning, and he had already sent Android‐9 and Android‐18 into hiding deep within the river, masking their heat signatures.
Sure enough, only minutes after he woke and began preparing, the alarm of the shelter blared.
Clang! Clang! Clang!
Sirens wailed, and what seemed like searchlights swept the skies!
Renji rushed outside just in time to see numerous Dragoons streaking across the night sky, each carrying Sentinel riders.
Everything happened so fast, their weapons lit up the darkness, unleashing a storm of bullets and projectiles toward the shelter.
Bang! Bang! Bang!
Renji ducked behind cover, readying himself to join the battle once the Sentinels dropped. But then something strange happened.
The bullets and projectiles froze in mid‐air.
"Huh?"
Renji’s eyes widened as the deadly rain of bullets hovered motionless above the shelter. Slowly, the glowing rounds dissolved into harmless sparks.
Finally, he realized what was going on!
"This place... it has a barrier? A force field?" he whispered, stunned.
The ground trembled as the Dragoons circled overhead, searching for a weakness!
This time, Renji’s heart pounded.
"W‐what the..."

chapters.title: Chapter 272: Renji’s Scheme and the Hidden Enemies
paragraphs: Thud! Thud! Thud!
The bullets dissolved into sparks, and not a single projectile managed to pass through it!
"How is this possible?" Renji couldn’t believe such a thing existed.
Soon, the Dragoons circled overhead, searching for a weakness in the barrier deployed.
He had been expecting the defenders to panic, but they were actually strong enough to stop the advance... It was no wonder they survived the Global Events that had been done so far!
Then, what happened next left him stunned.
From the main building, five massive figures emerged. They were modified Sentinels! There he saw the painted names on their chests.
They seemed to be called X‐02 through X‐06...
Renji watched as their eyes glowed while marching forward... Each of them was equipped with a familiar plasma rifles.
Without hesitation, they raised their weapons and unleashed streams of searing energy into the sky.
The beams tore through the night, striking the Dragoons perfect! Their accuracy couldn’t be compared to humans at all!
Renji couldn’t help but feel excited after seeing this.
’They actually reprogrammed Sentinels... and armed them with plasma rifles?’
He thought that he was special. He had Android 9 and 18 on his side, and he was lucky to be able to control them after fixing them in the junkyard.
However, this shelter proved him wrong.
Soon, he watched as the defenders of the shelter joined in!
Survivors lined the walls, rifles in hand, firing organized bursts at the incoming riders!
Bang! Bang! Bang!
Their shots were all calculated, aimed to suppress and weaken the enemy formations.
Renji could tell that they had practiced a lot! They must have a huge supply of ammunition that allowed them to be familiar with such a strategy.
"Just how rich is this shelter anyway? Everyone has a rifle... They’re not caring about having empty magazines... They have this barrier and the Modified Sentinels. Seriously..."
Then Renji noticed something even more remarkable.
Across the perimeter, survivors deployed compact devices!
Apparently, they were portable disruptor field units.
Whom~
A strange blast of energy came out from each of them!
At first, the Dragoons seemed unaffected, their systems compensating for the interference. But as dozens of disruptors activated simultaneously, the effect multiplied.
The sky filled with static.
The Dragoons’ signals halted... Engines started failing, and just like that, one by one, the machines began to lose control.
Renji’s eyes widened as the aerial units wobbled, then plummeted.
Crash! Crash! Crash!
The Dragoons slammed into the ground with their riders thrown violently from their seats...
Sparks erupted as circuits overloaded, leaving the once‐fearsome machines twitching helplessly in the dirt!
Renji scanned the battlefield...
This shelter was just too weird. Before this, he had been expecting the survivors to fight against the A.I. Army with various gene skills.
He believed that they would actually unleash mystical powers like fireballs, telekinesis, beast summons, and more... but none came.
There was no magical Gene Skills here, no supernatural tricks. Everything was achieved through advanced technology and combat tactics!
The plasma rifles, the disruptor fields, the reprogrammed Sentinels... all of it played a huge role!
And just like that, the battle was won.
Renji exhaled slowly, his heart pounding... Finally, he understood why these people seemed unafraid of anything.
"They don’t need mystical powers, huh..." he whispered.
"They have the strength... the technology... to fight back."
Just like that, he watched the defenders stand tall, as they rested for a bit before helping the Modified Sentinels collect the wreckage...
Renji’s disbelief turned into awe.
This shelter was thriving, armed with the kind of power that could challenge the A.I. Army head‐on.
Meanwhile, as the wreckage of the Dragoons was being cleared, one figure remained unnoticed in the chaos.
A lone A.I. Army’s Sentinel has been scouting the shelter from a distance.
When its allies fell, the machine did not engage further. Instead, it began to back away slowly, retreating into the night.
But as soon as it moved away, two more figures slowly moved.
It was Augustine and Russel, the scouts of New Haven‐45.
Equipped with advanced camouflage gear from Kai’s Superior Grade Stealth Gift Pack, their outlines blurred into the shadows, allowing them to move unseen.
They exchanged a quick glance... this was their chance. If they could follow the Sentinel, they might finally uncover the location of the A.I. Army’s base in this region.
They moved silently, keeping their distance as the Sentinel retreated.
The machine’s movements were fast, but cautious, as if aware it was being watched.
Yet Augustine and Russel’s gear held, masking their heat signatures and muffling their steps.
Hours passed as they trailed the Sentinel across rugged terrain...
Finally, the machine ascended a narrow path that wound up a mountain.
At the summit, a villa came into view... It was an elegant structure that seemed out of place in the war‐torn landscape.
Russel frowned beneath his visor.
"A villa? That doesn’t make sense. Why would the A.I. Army use this as a base?"
Augustine was also curious. "Look closer."
As they observed, several Spyder Units crawled out from the villa’s gates, their mechanical legs clicking against the stone.
The units dispersed quickly, scuttling down the mountain in different directions.
Russel was shocked. "Wait... They’re deploying scouts... from here?"
The realization struck them both at once. The villa was not the true base... it was a front, a disguise meant to mislead. The mountain itself seemed to be the base itself!
Beneath its surface, away from the eyes of the public, lay the real operations of the A.I. Army!
Augustine whispered, "This isn’t just a villa. The entire mountain is a camouflage base."
They watched as the Sentinel entered the villa, disappearing behind its gates...
Soon, the Spyder Units continued to pour out... The scale of the operation was staggering!
Russel tightened his grip on his rifle.
"We can’t attack this. Not with our current force. But knowing the location... the distance... the scale of their operations... it changes everything."
Augustine nodded grimly. "We’ll report back. Kai needs to know about this place... This mountain isn’t just a stronghold... It’s a fortress hidden in plain sight."

chapters.title: Chapter 274: The Recruit and the New A.I. Units
paragraphs: "Hmm? Aetherium Ore? This is the first time I heard something like this." Victor muttered softly.
[ You have discovered Aetherium Ore! ]
[ Grade: Rare Mineral ]

[ Description: A mineral produced through Anima’s modification of natural iron ores. The altered composition crystallizes into a dense alloy capable of amplifying energy conduction far beyond ordinary metals. Highly compatible with plasma weapon systems, barrier reinforcement modules, and advanced weapon repairs. ]
[ Note: Refinement requires specialized machinery. Improper handling may destabilize its lattice structure, causing hazardous energy discharge. ]
Victor’s eyes lingered on the glowing blue screen until it faded from view.
"Whew~"
He let out a slow breath... He was fascinated with the discovery but also frustrated with how limited his skill was.
"This ore... it’s extraordinary," he admitted as he checked all the corners of the ore in his hands before putting it back on the table.
"But my Appraisal Skill isn’t high enough. I can’t unlock all its secrets. What I saw was already valuable, but I know there’s more hidden within it."

Of course, his Appraisal was already Level 6... However, it was not enough to see through all of it. He even guessed that if his skill was just one level lower, he wouldn’t be able to find out what it was.
Then, he explained what he learned to others.
Marissa also felt that there was more to it than that...

"Even so, the information we gained is significant. Aetherium Ore... produced by Anima’s modification of iron. That explains its strange energy signature. If the A.I. Army is transporting this, it means they’re probably reinforcing their bases... or maybe they’re making a new type of machine. "

Victor nodded. "That’s possible. But since we’ll get a lot of these with Renji’s help, we’ll need someone skilled enough to process them. We should use it for ourselves, but without proper refinement, it’s just a dangerous lump of mineral."
"But if handled correctly... it could strengthen our walls, enhance our weapons, maybe even give us the edge against that mountain fortress."
"I can help with the refinement!" Renji volunteered.
Russel nodded. "Well, you’ve already proven you can repair androids. Maybe you can handle this ore too."
Augustine gave a reluctant nod. "Then perhaps we should forgive him. If he’s willing to work for us, we should give him the chance."
After a few more persuasions, they decided to take in Renji but not invite him to Kai’s Guild, Codebreakers.
"Renji, call your androids. We’ll allow them here, but under strict watch. And as for you... you’ll work for us for at least two months. You still lured those Dragoons to attack us."

Renji looked at them apologetically and nodded. He didn’t really mind staying in the shelter for a long time. The barrier system they used intrigued him deeply—it was unlike anything he had seen before.
"If I prove my loyalty, is it possible to join your Guild?" he asked carefully.
Victor was taken aback. He hadn’t expected Renji to ask that outright. For a moment, he hesitated, then admitted, "That’s not up to us alone to decide. But... we’ll see after you show your worth."
In the meantime, while they were dealing with Renji, the Blue Grass Shelter became busy...
It was unlike most survivor shelters.
It was small, only thirty‐two people in total, but its strength came from the leadership of three foreign Survivors who, like Kai, had arrived from another world.
There were six Foreign Survivors here, but Steven, Vera, and Juno led the group.
Steven, whose Iron Will Talent made him nearly unbreakable in battle and also tasked with the defense of the shelter.
Vera, gifted with the Alchemist Talent, had become the heart of their potion production.
And there was Juno, with his Telekinesis Talent, and the most versatile among them.
His Gene Skills amplified his control, allowing him to manipulate weapons, tools, and even enemy projectiles in battle. He was capable of both offense and defense within the shelter.

Together, these three had turned Blue Grass Shelter into a vital hub for the Codebreakers Guild. Their focus was on making the Soul‐Booster Potion production more efficient. Recently, they had begun setting up an assembly line system...

Vera arranged a small group to focus on brewing. Then, there was Steven’s team, managing the logistics and defense, while Juno and her team handled delicate transfers or the collection of ingredients. With this system, they could produce potions in bulk, supplying Kai’s guild with enough to sustain long campaigns against the A.I. Army.
At this time, the survivors were busy with this work when a message arrived through the Guild Chat.
Kai was coming. And he wasn’t alone... he was being chased by five enemies. Humans, not A.I.
Steven immediately ordered preparations.
"If they’re assassins, they’ll try to strike fast. Everyone, arm up. We’ll defend the shelter."
The defenders took positions, rifles and grenades ready.
But before Kai even reached the gates, another threat appeared.
From the treelines... Several C‐Grade Sentinels emerged...
These humanoid machines carried rifles, and they seemed to be moving fast.
Furthermore, they seemed to be more coordinated than before.
Bang! Bang! Bang!
Just like that, gunfire erupted as the Sentinels advanced!
The defenders of Blue Grass Shelter fought back with everything they had. Thanks to Kai’s earlier support, they were equipped with advanced gear and weapons.
They had Portable disruptor field units that scrambled the Sentinels’ targeting systems.
Sensor‐disrupting smoke grenades that cloaked the defenders in thick cover.
Flashbang grenades also disoriented the machines, buying precious seconds while decoy emitter devices projected false signals, drawing enemy fire away from the shelter walls!
And of course, rifles and grenade launchers gave them the firepower to punch through the Sentinels’ armor!
"Destroy them fast! We need to finish them before Kai arrives!"
The battle was fierce. Steven stood at the front, his Iron Will Talent allowing him to tank hits that would have dropped lesser fighters.
Vera stayed behind the lines and soon distributed the Gene Stimulant that they received from Kai!
Of course, other potions were also given to wounded defenders, and stamina boosters reached those who needed them most.
"Don’t hesitate! Trust the disruptor and the smokescreen!"
Juno’s telekinesis turned the tide more than once... rifles were suddenly ripped from enemy hands, grenades redirected mid‐air, and barricades were suddenly capable of blocking bullets!
"I can’t hold this for long! Finish them!" Juno said as her Spirit Energy was being consumed really fast!
Even with their coordination, the Sentinels weren’t easy to take down...
The defenders knew that this would still take time to completely eliminate them...
Then came the signal... Kai was close.
Since they couldn’t afford to send their forces, they immediately signalled for Atom to assist him!
Soon, the A‐Grade Sentinel, Kai’s most powerful android, was dispatched immediately.
Atom’s arrival would give Kai the support he needed against the assassins chasing him.
But as Atom left the shelter, something else stirred...
Crack... Crack...
The ground trembled. At first, the defenders thought it was artillery fire.
But then the soil cracked, and metallic drills burst upward!
Bang! Bang!
"Drillers?"
"Wait... I read about them in the Guild Chat!"
"Haa! Digger Units!? Shit!"
"Careful! They might release the bombers!"
Indeed, what had showed up was the Digger Units.
These were new A.I. soldiers, unlike anything they had faced before.
Their heads were massive drill‐like constructs, designed to pierce soil, rock, and concrete.
As the drills broke the surface, hatches opened along their chassis!
From within, swarms of insect‐like machines poured out... Bomber Swarmers.
They had already been informed about their existence but seeing them now made them nervous!
The swarmers skittered or flew across the ground with their bodies glowing faintly with unstable energy.
They were living bombs, designed to rush defenders and detonate on impact!
"Bomber Swarmers!" Juno shouted, her telekinesis already flinging debris to block their advance.
Boom! Boom! Boom!
She was able to hit many of them and soon, explosions rocked the battlefield as the swarmers hurled themselves at barricades, detonating in bursts of fire and shrapnel.
The defenders scrambled, using rifles and grenades to thin the swarm, but the sheer numbers were overwhelming.
Steven gritted his teeth, standing firm against the chaos.
"Hold the line! Smoke Grenades! More of them! Hurry! Let them hit the buildings, avoid them if you can’t bring them down!"
Steven’s eyes locked then on Hans, another foreign survivor.
Hans carried the Superior Talent called Quick Feet, a gift that made him untouchable in speed but left him fragile in defense.
He hated fighting up front, since his low pain tolerance was making every wound a risk.
Still, Steven’s command was firm. "Hans, deal with the Diggers!"
Hans swallowed hard, then nodded.
He slung his grenade launcher over his shoulder and sprinted out of the shelter.
His movements blurred, and he was faster than the Sentinels could track.
In seconds, he was already at the perimeter, avoiding all the explosions, preparing to unleash firepower directly on the drilling machines!
