chapters.title: Chapter 276: The Rep Store
paragraphs: The grass field was damaged by the explosions. It seemed that almost half of it was destroyed.
"Don’t worry... They grow quite easily, Kai." Vera reassured.
"Is that so? Then that’s perfect." Kai replied as he used his Keen Sense once more.
Soon, he heaved a sigh of relief... "I can’t sense any more A.I. soldiers around." Kai muttered as he sat down heavily on the wreckage of a fallen Sentinel.
The battlefield, or rather, the shelter itself, was in ruins. Barricades were shattered, bunkers were scorched, and the once‐calm grass fields were torn apart by drills and explosions.
Still, the survivors of Blue Grass Shelter were alive, and that alone felt like a miracle.
Groans and cries of pain echoed across the yard.

Vera swiftly moved with two of her assistants as they rushed to the injured. She carried pre‐prepared stimulants and healing concoctions, applying them quickly to stabilize wounds. "Pressure here... keep him conscious! Don’t let her move that leg, it’s fractured!" she ordered.
Steven also helped drag the wounded back under cover while Juno, drained from his telekinesis, leaned against a wall but still used his ability to lift debris off trapped survivors.
Even Hans, trembling from exhaustion, carried bandages and water to those who couldn’t walk.
Only once the bleeding was stopped and the worst injuries stabilized did the survivors turn their attention to the wreckage.
"Loot everything," Steven commanded, his tone grim. "Every scrap of metal, every rifle, every core. Strip the Sentinels, dismantle the Diggers... don’t leave a single part behind."
Just like that, they pried open shattered chassis, pulled out intact circuits, and stacked rifle parts into crates.
The Bomber Swarmers left behind scorched fragments of their unstable cores, which Vera quickly ordered collected.
"Even fragments of their energy cells can be studied... We might craft shock mines or portable charges." Vera muttered, which shocked Kai as he didn’t expect that she could be this resourceful.
However, he recalled that she was indeed not a mechanic like Victor but instead, a true Alchemist! Her view on materials brought by the A.I. Army was vastly different from a mechanic’s perspective.
She certainly could do a lot more things than he was aware of.
Meanwhile, Hans crouched beside the wreckage of a Digger.
Its drill head was massive, and still faintly glowing from friction...

"These drills..." he muttered, running his hand along the steel. "They’re designed to pierce reinforced bunkers. If we can mount them, we could dig tunnels beneath enemy patrol routes... or even carve out underground shelters."
Of course, he had no idea how they could make such a thing but he believed that Kai had people in other shelters who could make it happen.
Juno agreed after hearing it.

"Well... That might be possible." He muttered as he used his telekinesis to lift a broken drill segment onto a cart. "Imagine a network of escape tunnels. If the A.I. Army ever overwhelms us, we could vanish underground. Or use them to flank their bases."
Steven grinned despite his exhaustion. "Exactly. Repurpose their weapons into our tools. That’s how we survive. But who knows... We might have an escape route already."

As he said this, he looked at the holes created by the Diggers. Below their shelter, there might be a network of tunnels already. Perhaps, they could use this tunnel and block off the ones they didn’t need.
However, they also realized that it could be dangerous for them since if the enemies somehow noticed their tunnels and they had to fight underground, they would be at a disadvantage.
"Fighting underground using guns and explosives wouldn’t end well for us." Steven muttered as he imagined how the battle would go... He knew that their eardrums would surely rupture if that happened.
Nonetheless, this matter had to be reconsidered by the leaders.
Still, they had to come up with a solution to deal with the Diggers.
After all, they couldn’t let this happen again.
"If they drill into our rooms while we’re sleeping, that would be a disaster." Hans muttered.
"Yes. We need better ways to detect them. But don’t worry, I have a solution." Kai replied as he heard them talking.
Hearing this, the others didn’t immediately ask.
"Haha! Then we don’t have to be worried anymore!"
"You’re the best, Sir Kai!"
Just like that, they continued dismantling...
Even Atom assisted, tearing apart Digger frames, separating usable alloys from metal scrap.
Kai supervised, his Keen Sense guiding him to components that still held energy.
He was also curious if Atom would find that mysterious black ball once again and absorb it.
However, Atom didn’t do anything other than dismantle the Diggers.
Soon, Kai also worked and informed the others what are the parts they should take care of.
"These stabilizers," Kai muttered after an appraisal. Then, he assisted in identifying the decent parts of the Diggers and Sentinels.
"These C-Grade Cores are damaged. Be careful."
"Handle the blades with gloves. They’re sharp."
"These metal panels can be used to reinforce the wall."
"We can repurpose these blades as weapons or projectiles."
"Should we make a better helmet with these Sentinel heads?"
Just like that, they made various suggestions about the items they collected.
Hans also suggested an idea that everyone had already considered.
"What if we use the drills to dig storage vaults or bunkers beneath the shelter?"
Steven shook his head. "We already thought of that. But it’s dangerous... Let’s just wait for Kai’s solution against the Diggers."
Hans could only scratch his head as he continued working.
The survivors worked tirelessly, stripping rifles from Sentinels, salvaging armor plating, and hauling drill heads into storage. They debated uses for each part...
By nightfall, the shelter was littered with organized piles of loot.
At this time, Kai decided to recheck his Reputation Store. After purchasing the Neural Gear for 100 Reputation Points a couple of days ago, the Store should’ve refreshed by now.
[ Reputation Store Accessed ]
[ Current Reputation Points: 101 ]
[ Store Inventory - Weekly Rotation ]
[ Pain Suppression Injector ] [ 3/3 ]
[ Cost: 5 RP ]
[ Effect: Temporarily blocks pain signals in the nervous system for 30 minutes. Neutralizes discomfort without affecting mobility or awareness. ]
[ Cellular Regeneration Serum ] [ 2/2 ]
[ Cost: 6 RP ]
[ Effect: Accelerates healing of internal injuries and fractures. Cuts recovery time by 99%. Single‐use, but highly effective. ]

chapters.title: Chapter 277: The Items and the Global Event
paragraphs: Kai stared at the refreshed store list.
"Pain Suppression Injector, huh..."

He knew that they’d be useful for keeping fighters on their feet, but it seemed risky if they were used for that purpose. After all, it only blocks pain. It should be used in surgery or something similar instead of combat.
As for the second item, he couldn’t help but nod in satisfaction.
"Cellular Regeneration Serum... now this is rare. Cuts recovery time almost completely. If we stock these, even serious injuries won’t keep our people down for long."

Although leveling up was also a way to recover from physical injuries, it would be harder and harder to happen at higher levels. They needed such serums, medicine, or even a potion to get healed in many cases.
After all, shelters with skilled doctors wouldn’t be easy to find.
Nonetheless, Kai didn’t purchase them yet.
He scrolled further, noticing three more items now available.
[ Spirit Recovery Drink] [ 10/10 ]
[ Cost: 1 RP ]
[ Effect: A refined liquid stored in a sealed vial. When consumed, it replenishes Spirit Energy instantly, restoring 50 points. ]
[ Shockwave Baton ] [ 2/2 ]
[ Cost: 10 RP ]

[ Effect: A compact weapon that releases a directed electrical burst. On activation, it releases a burst in a cone up to 10 meters, short‐circuiting exposed mechanical units and disabling their systems. ]
[ Magnetic Pulse Mine ] [ 5/5 ]
[ Cost: 5 RP ]
[ Effect: A mine that detonates with a violent magnetic surge. On activation, it overloads circuits, fries processors, and permanently disables mechanical units within a 20-meter radius. ]
"Spirit Recovery Drink... ten vials, only one point each."
Kai paused for a moment as he saw it. "That’s quite decent for 50 Spirit Points. But isn’t this a bit too big?"
He shifted to the next entry. "Shockwave Baton... Ten points each. A close‐range weapon... but it disables circuits within ten meters. Interesting..."
Finally, his gaze settled on the last item. "Magnetic Pulse Mine for only five points. This is nice... It might work against the Diggers."
He couldn’t take his eyes off of it.
"It’s quite destructive... It should be a proper countermeasure against these machines."
Kai felt satisfied with the current set of items being sold.

Still, the Spirit Drink, worth 1 Reputation Point each, wasn’t really worth it since he already had access to Soul Booster. It was only 10mL and provides 30 Spirit Points already. However, the Spirit Drink was about 100mL.
In the end, he decided to stick with this shelter’s potions.
So, he instead purchased one Cellular Regeneration Serum, one Shockwave Baton, and three Magnetic Pulse Mine.
[ Current Reputation Points: 70 ]
Kai then appraised the Mine and Baton once again for a complete description. After all, the ones in the store were just too short for the buyer to have an idea.
[ You have discovered Shockwave Baton! ]
[ Grade: Specialized Weapon ]

[ Description: A compact melee weapon designed to release a directed electrical burst. On activation, the baton projects a cone of high‐voltage discharge up to 10 meters, short‐circuiting exposed mechanical units and disabling their systems. It can withstand repeated strikes without degrading. ]

[ Note: Contains 5 internal charge cells. Each cell provides one full discharge before requiring replacement. Rechargeable with standard energy packs, though efficiency decreases after prolonged use. ]
"So it’s five charges, huh... Not bad." Kai muttered as he saw the description.
[ You have discovered Magnetic Pulse Mine! ]
[ Grade: Anti‐Mechanical Explosive ]

[ Description: An easily deployable mine engineered to detonate with a violent magnetic surge, mostly affecting mechanical units rather than living beings. Once triggered, it overloads circuits, fries processors, and permanently disables mechanical units within a 20‐meter radius. ]
[ Note: Single‐use device. Each mine contains a sealed magnetic core that destabilizes upon activation. Safe handling requires insulated gloves. Accidental discharge may damage nearby equipment. ]
"I see... So it works best on machines, not on mutants or other survivors." Kai muttered.
The next morning, Kai stood before the survivors. The memory of drills tearing through their defenses, bypassing their walls, still weighed heavily on him.

"We can’t let the Diggers breach us again," he said. "Just like what you said yesterday, if they drill into our rooms while we’re sleeping, it’ll be a disaster. First... we need a way to detect them before they break through."
He walked across the ruined yard, pointing at the shattered earth.
"Their weakness is vibration. Every time they tunnel, the ground trembles. If we can sense those vibrations early, we’ll know exactly where they’re coming from."
Kai held up a salvaged Sentinel stabilizer, stripped from last night’s wreckage.

"These stabilizers still hold energy. If we rewire them into the shelter’s foundation, they can act as seismic sensors. Whenever the ground shifts unnaturally, the stabilizers will resonate. We’ll hear it, or even see it as a signal."
Vera’s eyes widened. "So... like an early warning system?"
Kai nodded. "Exactly. A detection grid. We’ll embed the stabilizers beneath the walls and connect them to a simple alarm circuit. Even a faint tremor will trigger it."
Need to say, Kai was referring to his Superior Grade Shelter Gift Pack’s Perimeter Alarm System Set, a compact device designed to detect movement and trigger alerts through the nodes it had.
Hans scratched his head, intrigued. "That means we’ll know the Diggers are coming before they break through."

"Right," Kai replied. "And once we know, we can prepare countermeasures... grenades, barricades, traps, or even evacuations into safer tunnels. But still, the best answer would be the activation of the Disruptor Units. The key is awareness."
Well, the Portable Disruptor Field Unit couldn’t be activated automatically. Because of that, the alarm system was still necessary.
Juno felt satisfied with this. At the very least, they’d no longer be surprised.
"It’s not a weapon, but it gives us time. That’s what we lacked before."
Kai nodded. "That’s right... We don’t need to fight them underground. We just need to know they’re coming. If we can detect them, we can control the battlefield instead of being ambushed."
Soon, the group started working on the installation.
However, as Kai returned to his room and was about to use his Neural Gear to enter the Perfect World, a Global System Notification appeared!

chapters.title: Chapter 278: Global Event and the Gene Trader
paragraphs: [ Global Event is Here! ]
[ Upcoming Special Operation: Black Market Auction ]
[ Countdown: 3 Days ]
[ Duration: 2 Days ]

[ Objective: Survivors who acquire Auction Tokens from Gene Traders before the deadline may enter the continent‐wide Black Market Auction. Tokens serve as entry passes, granting access to hidden bidding halls where rare items, genetic resources, and forbidden technologies are exchanged. ]
[ Failure Condition: Survivors without Auction Tokens are barred from entry. ]
[ Note: Auction halls are neutral zones under Gene Trader protection. Combat is restricted inside. ]

[ Currency: Survivor Medals will serve as the primary bidding currency. Survivors lacking sufficient medals may exchange resources with Gene Traders, but conversion rates will vary depending on the rarity and quality of the items offered. ]
[ Special Reminder: Auction Tokens can only be purchased from Gene Traders within 3 days of this announcement. Survivors who fail to obtain tokens will be excluded from the event. ]
Kai was stunned as he read the notification line by line.
"Black Market Auction... Gene Traders again."
He didn’t expect that there would be such an event at all. He thought that the Global Event was only meant to fight against the A.I. Army.
There was actually a Survivor-Only Event like this.
"Tokens within three days, or you’re locked out. And the bidding currency... Survivor Medals."
Kai wryly smiled as he knew that he might have a lot of them right now, but he believed that some others could have more of them.
Still, the fact that there was no level restriction meant that the number of participants would be incredibly huge.
Kai closed the window, but the murmurs outside his door caught his attention.
Vera’s voice was tense. "Three days? How are we supposed to find a Gene Trader in time? It’s been weeks since the last one appeared."

Steven’s reply was equally worried. "Exactly. They vanish after a while, and no one knows where they’ll show up next. We can’t just sit here and hope one strolls near our shelter. We can’t miss this opportunity..."
Kai listened silently and nodded.
Their fear was justified. The Gene Traders were cloaked enigmas, appearing in forgotten alleys, ruined tunnels, or dark caves.
Survivors stumbled upon them by chance, never by certainty. Missing the window meant exclusion from the auction... and exclusion meant losing access to items that could shift the balance of survival.
He rose from his chair, stepping toward the door.
’They’re right,’he thought grimly.
’Although there’s one Gene Trader near New Haven-45, that’s only one, and there might be a limit to the number of invitations he can sell.’
Furthermore, Kai knew that traveling that far wouldn’t be a good idea for this shelter here. They could not leave this place without proper protection.
Soon, Kai opened the door, meeting Vera and Steven’s anxious gazes.
"We’ll have to search for a Gene Trader..."
The two nodded as they also planned to start searching right away.
The group was quickly organized.
Kai insisted on splitting into four separate search parties to cover more ground.
He himself would go alone, confident in his own survival skills and detection abilities.
Hans, with his Quick Feet Talent, was also assigned to scout independently in the west.
Vera led a small team composed of Steven and two other survivors, while Juno took three more under his command.
As for the defense of the shelter, Atom would stay here to lead the group of Survivors.
Meanwhile, Kai equipped each group with radios for communication, sensor‐disrupting smoke grenades for emergency escapes, and advanced camouflage gear.
After that, every survivor was clad in the same slim, dark suit with sealed helmets.
No face or skin could be seen, and the gear’s layered design blocked most heat signatures and detection scans.
As they stood together, they looked less like desperate survivors and more like assassins preparing for a covert operation.
"This looks super cool..."
"Hahaha... That’s true. It adjusted to my size as well."
"I thought this helmet will be suffocating, it actually feels really good."
"Maybe we can also use this for underwater operation or something?"
"Don’t try... It might be hard to swim with this."
"It’s still heavy. It just feels light since we’re level 20..."
Kai smiled as he listened to their conversation.
"Alright... Stay in contact. Report any signs immediately," Kai ordered as he used the radio for communication.
"Remember, the Gene Traders don’t linger in bright places... They’re somewhere in the dark. If you find one, secure the location and wait. Don’t engage recklessly."
With that, the teams dispersed into different directions...
Kai headed north, guided by Vera’s earlier mention of an abandoned town in that direction.
In less than an hour, he was able to find collapsed buildings, rusted vehicles half‐buried in ash, and streets overtaken by weeds.
"So it’s here..."
He moved silently with his camouflage suit blending into the dim light...
"This will be a long search," he muttered under his breath, scanning the horizon.
The Gene Traders were elusive, appearing only in hidden corners where few dared to tread. He expected hours of wandering, perhaps even days.
But fortune seemed to favor him.
As he approached the outskirts of the abandoned town, his passive Keen Sense skill triggered.
A faint ripple of energy brushed against his mind...
Kai froze as he recognized that it was a Gene Trader’s aura.

"There’s one here..." he whispered. He actually didn’t expect to sense this at all. After all, he had never sensed a Gene Trader before. At the very least, he needed to be within three meters of the Gene Trader to detect its unique Aura.
"I guess my Keen Sense is just that good right now," Kai muttered as he advanced cautiously, following the sensation.
Soon, he spotted a cloaked figure standing beside a pile of crates and bags within an abandoned building.
It was the unmistakable silhouette of a Gene Trader.
The merchant’s hood concealed its face, like every other Gene Trader.
Kai couldn’t help but smile as he had found one so easily...
But then, his Keen Sense also picked up a movement nearby.

He crouched instantly, activating his camouflage to its fullest. Through the faint distortion, he realized he wasn’t alone. Someone was already there... another survivor was actually beside the Gene Trader, and he was also using a Stealth Skill!

chapters.title: Chapter 279: The Level 80 and the Gene Trader
paragraphs: Kai’s eyes focused as he studied the figure beside the Gene Trader.
His Keen Sense had failed to detect the man until he was almost within reach.
That alone told him the stranger was using some kind of stealth skill, or perhaps an ability that blocked detection outright.
For now, Kai decided against radioing the others.
He might alert the man to the noise, and of course, if he announced this too soon, they would all converge here, and if tokens were limited, it would be a problem.
Better to let them search for a few more hours... maybe they’d stumble upon other Gene Traders.
For now, he just focused on the man before him.
As he waited for about ten minutes, Kai soon realized that their transaction had ended...
The cloaked merchant stored the crystal once again, and soon, the man started fixing his baggage...
Then, as if sensing Kai’s presence, the stranger turned. His eyes met Kai’s through the dim light, and he smiled.
"You there... don’t worry. I can tell you’re human. I won’t hurt you."
That was definitely a good greeting...
Kai hesitated as he held his baton... if it didn’t work, he was also ready to activate his Gene Weapon.
However, the man’s tone was calm, almost reassuring. After a moment, Kai deactivated his camouflage and stepped forward, revealing himself.

The man nodded approvingly. "I just bought a few things from this Gene Trader. Nothing more." His gaze also studied Kai more closely. Then he gave a small nod, as if confirming something. "You’re a Foreign Survivor, aren’t you?"
Kai frowned. "You can tell?"

"Yes," the man replied without hesitation. "Only Level 80 survivors of this land can approach the Gene Traders. Since you’re not even Level 40, you must be one of the Foreign Survivors. You all are blessed."
Kai’s eyes widened.
He didn’t expect that this man could tell that his level hadn’t reached 40.
’Is there a specific aura about them? Or maybe his Gene Skill allowed him to do so...’He mused.

He had known the locals couldn’t approach the Gene Traders without meeting certain requirements, but he hadn’t expected the threshold to be Level 80. That was an absurdly high ceiling, far beyond what most survivors could reach quickly.
Still, he felt a flicker of relief. The man trusted him enough to speak openly, and that trust mattered.
The stranger extended his hand. "Vernon Leo. From Cameron City."
Kai studied him carefully before shaking his hand.

Vernon was tall, broad‐shouldered, with really caucasian features framed by short dark hair. His armor was practical but well‐crafted to fit his body. It had metallic plates that bore faint insignias of a lion’s head... most likely the mark of his faction.
"Kai," he introduced himself simply.
Inwardly, Kai searched his memory.

He couldn’t recall much about the Leo Faction in Cameron City. He had encountered Cancer, Aries, and even heard of Taurus, but the other zodiac factions hadn’t crossed his path. Cornelio of Aries had warned him about Cancer and Taurus, but never Leo.
That left Kai uncertain what to expect.
The two stood in silence for a moment before Vernon spoke again.
"Are you going to use the Gene Trader now? I just purchased various Gene Enhancements..."
Kai nodded, then he recalled something and asked carefully, "Right... Did you receive any notification about the Auction?"
Vernon shook his head. "No. Nothing like that..."
From here, Vernon guessed that it was a Foreign Survivor thing, so he didn’t ask.
Meanwhile, Kai’s suspicions were confirmed.
As expected, only Foreign Survivors like them get those invitations. The locals weren’t invited.
Vernon then reached into his pouch and pulled out a small token, handing it to Kai. "This is an invitation to Cameron City. If you ever visit, you can enter freely."
Kai was curious about this and inspected it for a moment...
"Ahem... I already have an invitation from Aries. I even visited Cameron some time ago."
Vernon’s eyes widened in surprise, then he chuckled.
"Aries? Impressive. I didn’t expect that. In that case..." He produced another token, this one etched with the lion insignia.
"This is for the Leo Shelter outside Cameron City, near the Grid Region. If you visit, you can trade there without heavy tolls or taxes. You’ll find many useful things."
Kai accepted the token, though he didn’t truly need it.
Still, he asked, "Why are you being so friendly? There must be a catch."

Vernon chuckled. "Well... There’s not really a catch. I just want you to view the Leo Faction positively. We’re not like Cancer or Taurus. We don’t thrive on manipulation or bloodshed... unless it’s against the enemies of humanity... If you remember us favorably, that’s enough."
Kai studied him for a long moment, then nodded. "Fair enough."
With that, Vernon adjusted his cloak and prepared to leave.
"I’ll be heading back... Take care, Kai. Perhaps we’ll meet again..."
Kai watched him disappear into the ruins, his figure faded into the shadows. He glanced down at the token in his hand, the lion even seemed like it had energy lingering on it.
"Leo Faction..." he murmured.
For now, he kept the token tucked safely away.
Kai stepped forward, the faint glow of the Gene Trader’s wares reflecting off his visor. The cloaked merchant raised a small, glowing purple sphere, its surface swirling with faint specks of light.
Immediately, a blue screen materialized before Kai’s eyes:
[ Gene Trader’s Store ]
[ Survivor Medal Items ] [ Energy Core Items ]
[ Item Conversion ] [ Auction Tokens ]
Kai’s brows furrowed. Two new tabs had appeared...
Item ConversionandAuction Tokens.
"So that’s how it works..." he muttered. He guessed the Item Conversion tab was meant for turning resources into Survivor Medals, while the Auction Token tab was where the entry passes were sold.
Without hesitation, Kai tapped onAuction Tokens.
The screen shifted, confirming only one item available...
"Nice..."

[ Auction Token: A sealed token inscribed with mysterious engravings. Grants entry into the Black Market Auction, a continent‐wide event where rare items, genetic resources, and forbidden technologies are bid upon. Without this token, entry is impossible. ]
[ Cost: 5,000 Experience Points ]
[ Stock: 10 ]
Kai was shocked.
"Experience Points... not Survivor Medals." He had expected the price to be steep, but this was heavier than he thought.
Still, there was no choice. Without the token, he’d be excluded.
He sighed, then confirmed the purchase.
[ You have purchased Auction Token. ]
[ 5,000 Experience Points deducted. ]
The glowing sphere dimmed slightly as one token vanished from the stock.
"Good. At least I secured one."
He then tapped back to theSurvivor Medal Itemstab.
He just wanted to see if there were any changes...
[ Super Gene Enhancement Serum: A basic serum that slightly improves genetic compatibility, granting small boosts to overall stats and a high chance of awakening a Gene Skill.
Cost: 4 Survivor Medals ]
[ Alpha Gene Enhancement Serum: A rare genetic resource that grants balanced boosts to overall stats and provides a small chance of awakening a Gene Skill.
Cost: 4 Survivor Medals ]
[ Warrior Gene Enhancement Serum: A rare serum that focuses on greatly improving Physique and provides a small chance of awakening a Gene Skill.
Cost: 5 Survivor Medals ]

[ Mutagenic Gene Enhancement Serum: An unstable serum that grants massive boosts to overall stats but carries a high chance of mutation. Mutations may result in unpredictable abilities or severe drawbacks.
Cost: 1 Survivor Medal ]
Well, the only change was the fact that the Prime Gene Enhancement was replaced by Warrior Gene Enhancement, and it was even more expensive than before.
As for the Gene Skills, there were only slight changes.
[ Gene Skill Crystal (Low‐Grade): A crystal that awakens an active or passive gene skill. The ability varies depending on the user’s genetic state.
Cost: 5 Survivor Medals ]

[ Random Gene Skill Crystal (Low‐Grade): A crystal that triggers a random bodily adjustment or passive skill, often minor but useful. The awakened gene skill depends on prior enhancements. Cost: 4 Survivor Medals ]
[ Active Gene Skill Crystal (Mid‐Grade): A crystal that awakens a powerful Active Gene Skill. The ability differs for each user, influenced by their physique and gene enhancements taken.
Cost: 8 Survivor Medals ]
[ Passive Gene Skill Crystal (Mid‐Grade): A crystal that awakens a powerful Passive Gene Skill. Cost: 8 Survivor Medals ]
[ Random Gene Skill Crystal (Mid‐Grade): A crystal that awakens a powerful Random Gene Skill. Cost: 8 Survivor Medals ]
They had actually become more expensive!
Well, they must have better effects now, but Kai couldn’t just accept this.
Still, he wasn’t here for the Skills.
So after calming himself, he tapped onItem Conversion. A huge blank window appeared, waiting for input.
"Alright... let’s test this."
Without hesitation, Kai opened his inventory and placed one mountain bike into the conversion slot.
[ Item Conversion in Progress... ]
[ Result: Mountain Bike to 0.07 Points ]
[ Note: 1 Point = 1 Survivor Medal. Conversion incomplete. Withdrawals unavailable until full point is reached. ]
Kai frowned. "Only that much for a brand new bike? Well... Whatever..."
Well, he had an Infinite Gift Pack anyway, he might as well abuse it!
Furthermore, those in his Superior Grade Gift Packs could surely give him better conversion!

sentences.text: Kai’s eyes focused as he studied the figure beside the Gene Trader.
His Keen Sense had failed to detect the man until he was almost within reach.
That alone told him the stranger was using some kind of stealth skill, or perhaps an ability that blocked detection outright.
For now, Kai decided against radioing the others.
He might alert the man to the noise, and of course, if he announced this too soon, they would all converge here, and if tokens were limited, it would be a problem.
Better to let them search for a few more hours... maybe they’d stumble upon other Gene Traders.
For now, he just focused on the man before him.
As he waited for about ten minutes, Kai soon realized that their transaction had ended...
The cloaked merchant stored the crystal once again, and soon, the man started fixing his baggage...
Then, as if sensing Kai’s presence, the stranger turned.
His eyes met Kai’s through the dim light, and he smiled.
"You there... don’t worry.
I can tell you’re human.
I won’t hurt you."
That was definitely a good greeting...
Kai hesitated as he held his baton... if it didn’t work, he was also ready to activate his Gene Weapon.
However, the man’s tone was calm, almost reassuring.
After a moment, Kai deactivated his camouflage and stepped forward, revealing himself.
The man nodded approvingly.
"I just bought a few things from this Gene Trader.
Nothing more." His gaze also studied Kai more closely.
Then he gave a small nod, as if confirming something.
"You’re a Foreign Survivor, aren’t you?"
Kai frowned.
"You can tell?"
"Yes," the man replied without hesitation.
"Only Level 80 survivors of this land can approach the Gene Traders.
Since you’re not even Level 40, you must be one of the Foreign Survivors.
You all are blessed."
Kai’s eyes widened.
He didn’t expect that this man could tell that his level hadn’t reached 40.
’Is there a specific aura about them?
Or maybe his Gene Skill allowed him to do so...’He mused.
He had known the locals couldn’t approach the Gene Traders without meeting certain requirements, but he hadn’t expected the threshold to be Level 80.
That was an absurdly high ceiling, far beyond what most survivors could reach quickly.
Still, he felt a flicker of relief.
The man trusted him enough to speak openly, and that trust mattered.
The stranger extended his hand.
"Vernon Leo.
From Cameron City."
Kai studied him carefully before shaking his hand.
Vernon was tall, broad‐shouldered, with really caucasian features framed by short dark hair.
His armor was practical but well‐crafted to fit his body.
It had metallic plates that bore faint insignias of a lion’s head... most likely the mark of his faction.
"Kai," he introduced himself simply.
Inwardly, Kai searched his memory.
He couldn’t recall much about the Leo Faction in Cameron City.
He had encountered Cancer, Aries, and even heard of Taurus, but the other zodiac factions hadn’t crossed his path.
Cornelio of Aries had warned him about Cancer and Taurus, but never Leo.
That left Kai uncertain what to expect.
The two stood in silence for a moment before Vernon spoke again.
"Are you going to use the Gene Trader now?
I just purchased various Gene Enhancements..."
Kai nodded, then he recalled something and asked carefully, "Right...
Did you receive any notification about the Auction?"
Vernon shook his head.
"No.
Nothing like that..."
From here, Vernon guessed that it was a Foreign Survivor thing, so he didn’t ask.
Meanwhile, Kai’s suspicions were confirmed.
As expected, only Foreign Survivors like them get those invitations.
The locals weren’t invited.
Vernon then reached into his pouch and pulled out a small token, handing it to Kai.
"This is an invitation to Cameron City.
If you ever visit, you can enter freely."
Kai was curious about this and inspected it for a moment...
"Ahem...
I already have an invitation from Aries.
I even visited Cameron some time ago."
Vernon’s eyes widened in surprise, then he chuckled.
"Aries?
Impressive.
I didn’t expect that.
In that case..." He produced another token, this one etched with the lion insignia.
"This is for the Leo Shelter outside Cameron City, near the Grid Region.
If you visit, you can trade there without heavy tolls or taxes.
You’ll find many useful things."
Kai accepted the token, though he didn’t truly need it.
Still, he asked, "Why are you being so friendly?
There must be a catch."
Vernon chuckled.
"Well...
There’s not really a catch.
I just want you to view the Leo Faction positively.
We’re not like Cancer or Taurus.
We don’t thrive on manipulation or bloodshed... unless it’s against the enemies of humanity...
If you remember us favorably, that’s enough."
Kai studied him for a long moment, then nodded.
"Fair enough."
With that, Vernon adjusted his cloak and prepared to leave.
"I’ll be heading back...
Take care, Kai.
Perhaps we’ll meet again..."
Kai watched him disappear into the ruins, his figure faded into the shadows.
He glanced down at the token in his hand, the lion even seemed like it had energy lingering on it.
"Leo Faction..." he murmured.
For now, he kept the token tucked safely away.
Kai stepped forward, the faint glow of the Gene Trader’s wares reflecting off his visor.
The cloaked merchant raised a small, glowing purple sphere, its surface swirling with faint specks of light.
Immediately, a blue screen materialized before Kai’s eyes:
[ Gene Trader’s Store ]
[ Survivor Medal Items ] [ Energy Core Items ]
[ Item Conversion ] [ Auction Tokens ]
Kai’s brows furrowed.
Two new tabs had appeared...
Item ConversionandAuction Tokens.
"So that’s how it works..." he muttered.
He guessed the Item Conversion tab was meant for turning resources into Survivor Medals, while the Auction Token tab was where the entry passes were sold.
Without hesitation, Kai tapped onAuction Tokens.
The screen shifted, confirming only one item available...
"Nice..."
[ Auction Token: A sealed token inscribed with mysterious engravings.
Grants entry into the Black Market Auction, a continent‐wide event where rare items, genetic resources, and forbidden technologies are bid upon.
Without this token, entry is impossible. ]
[ Cost: 5,000 Experience Points ]
[ Stock: 10 ]
Kai was shocked.
"Experience Points... not Survivor Medals." He had expected the price to be steep, but this was heavier than he thought.
Still, there was no choice.
Without the token, he’d be excluded.
He sighed, then confirmed the purchase.
[ You have purchased Auction Token. ]
[ 5,000 Experience Points deducted. ]
The glowing sphere dimmed slightly as one token vanished from the stock.
"Good.
At least I secured one."
He then tapped back to theSurvivor Medal Itemstab.
He just wanted to see if there were any changes...
[ Super Gene Enhancement Serum: A basic serum that slightly improves genetic compatibility, granting small boosts to overall stats and a high chance of awakening a Gene Skill.
Cost: 4 Survivor Medals ]
[ Alpha Gene Enhancement Serum: A rare genetic resource that grants balanced boosts to overall stats and provides a small chance of awakening a Gene Skill.
Cost: 4 Survivor Medals ]
[ Warrior Gene Enhancement Serum: A rare serum that focuses on greatly improving Physique and provides a small chance of awakening a Gene Skill.
Cost: 5 Survivor Medals ]
[ Mutagenic Gene Enhancement Serum: An unstable serum that grants massive boosts to overall stats but carries a high chance of mutation.
Mutations may result in unpredictable abilities or severe drawbacks.
Cost: 1 Survivor Medal ]
Well, the only change was the fact that the Prime Gene Enhancement was replaced by Warrior Gene Enhancement, and it was even more expensive than before.
As for the Gene Skills, there were only slight changes.
[ Gene Skill Crystal (Low‐Grade): A crystal that awakens an active or passive gene skill.
The ability varies depending on the user’s genetic state.
Cost: 5 Survivor Medals ]
[ Random Gene Skill Crystal (Low‐Grade): A crystal that triggers a random bodily adjustment or passive skill, often minor but useful.
The awakened gene skill depends on prior enhancements.
Cost: 4 Survivor Medals ]
[ Active Gene Skill Crystal (Mid‐Grade): A crystal that awakens a powerful Active Gene Skill.
The ability differs for each user, influenced by their physique and gene enhancements taken.
Cost: 8 Survivor Medals ]
[ Passive Gene Skill Crystal (Mid‐Grade): A crystal that awakens a powerful Passive Gene Skill.
Cost: 8 Survivor Medals ]
[ Random Gene Skill Crystal (Mid‐Grade): A crystal that awakens a powerful Random Gene Skill.
Cost: 8 Survivor Medals ]
They had actually become more expensive!
Well, they must have better effects now, but Kai couldn’t just accept this.
Still, he wasn’t here for the Skills.
So after calming himself, he tapped onItem Conversion.
A huge blank window appeared, waiting for input.
"Alright... let’s test this."
Without hesitation, Kai opened his inventory and placed one mountain bike into the conversion slot.
[ Item Conversion in Progress... ]
[ Result: Mountain Bike to 0.07 Points ]
[ Note: 1 Point = 1 Survivor Medal.
Conversion incomplete.
Withdrawals unavailable until full point is reached. ]
Kai frowned.
"Only that much for a brand new bike?
Well...
Whatever..."
Well, he had an Infinite Gift Pack anyway, he might as well abuse it!
Furthermore, those in his Superior Grade Gift Packs could surely give him better conversion!

chapters.title: Chapter 280: The Item Conversion and the Return
paragraphs: Kai thought for a moment, then opened a Superior Transport Gift Pack... There were several items here but he started with the off‐road motorbike.
[ Item Conversion in Progress... ]
[ Result: Off Road Motorbike converted to 0.20 Points ]

Kai gently nodded at the result. "A brand new mountain bike from the Enhanced Transport Gift Pack gave me 0.07, but the Superior Transport Gift Pack’s off road motorbike converts to 0.20... Still, four motorbikes give a single point."
He was satisfied, but he wasn’t done. He wanted to test everything within the Superior Transport Gift Pack.
Next, he placed the fuel reserve containers into the slot.
[ Result: Fuel Reserve Container converted to 0.30 Points ]
Kai didn’t expect much from this, but the result was better than he thought.
"Not bad. Fuel has its value after all."
Next came the protective riding gear.
[ Result: Protective Riding Gear converted to 0.40 Points ]
Kai tilted his head. "Better than fuel and the mountain bike, but still not amazing."
Just like that, he worked on the repair kit with spare parts and the others.
[ Result: Repair Kit converted to 0.25 Points ]
[ Result: Collapsible Canoe converted to 0.35 Points ]
[ Result: Emergency Thruster Pack converted to 2.25 Points ]
Finally, he had to pause.
Kai’s eyes widened. "Now that’s insane. One thruster pack is worth more than ten motorbikes combined. The system clearly values high-tech gear for sure"
Finally, the compact grappling launcher.
[ Result: Compact Grappling Launcher converted to 2.25 Points ]
Kai grinned. "Another jackpot. Grappling launchers are actually similar in price... This is what I needed."
He quickly tallied the totals...
Off Road Motorbike: 0.20
Fuel Reserve Containers: 0.30
Protective Riding Gear: 0.40
Repair Kit: 0.25
Collapsible Canoe: 0.35
Emergency Thruster Pack: 2.25
Compact Grappling Launcher: 2.25
Total: 6.00 Points for one Superior Transport Gift Pack.
Kai was definitely satisfied.
"One Superior Transport Gift Pack is worth that much, huh... The thruster pack and grappling launcher carry the points here for sure. Without them, the rest is trash."
Now, when he moved on to the Weapon Gift Pack (Superior), he couldn’t help but realize how lucky he was!
Carbine Rifle: 0.80
Shotgun: 0.75
Spear: 0.40
Combat Knife: 0.35
Protective Vest: 0.70
Grenade Launcher: 1.50
Ammunition Crates: 2.00
Total: 6.50 Points.
Kai frowned. "Weapons don’t convert as well as Transport, but at least the grenade launcher and crates make up for it."

He then continued with the Stealth Gift Pack. This time, the total came to 5.70 Points, but the standout items were clear: the Disruptor Field Unit gave 1.30 Points, while the Advanced Camouflage Gear reached 1.40 Points.
Kai nodded, noting that stealth wasn’t bad, though only those two items truly carried the pack.
"Next..."
The Energy Gift Pack was soon converted to 5.70 Points. The portable fuel generator was the highest at 1.50 Points, followed by the solar panel set at 1.00 Points.
’Similar total points with Stealth Gift Pack, huh...’
Anyway, the Entertainment Gift Pack also totaled 6 Points.
The offline knowledge archive gave 1.20 Points, while the media tablet contributed 1.00 Points. Kai chuckled, amused that entertainment had some worth.
Then, the Food Gift Pack came to 5.80 Points. The hydroponic starter kit was the clear standout at 1.50 Points, with the portable cooking stove adding 1.20 Points.
Kai shrugged, thinking food was essential, but only hydroponics truly paid off in medals.
The Medical Gift Pack proved powerful, totaling 6.50 Points!
"Now, this isn’t that bad..."
The advanced surgical kit gave 1.90 Points, while the emergency defibrillator unit reached 1.30 Points...
’Six point fifty again... I wonder if this is the highest.’ Kai mused as he turned to the last three packs, Shelter Gift Pack, Survivor Tools Gift Pack and Water Gift Pack."

The Shelter Gift Pack reached 5.60 Points. The modular survival pod was the highest at 1.50 Points, followed by the perimeter alarm system at 1.20 Points. Kai nodded, satisfied that shelter gear was solid, with the pod being the best investment.
The Survival Tools Gift Pack totaled 7.00 Points, making it one of the strongest packs so far.
The portable drone scout was the star at 2.50 Points, while the navigation kit gave 1.80 Points. Kai smiled, realizing survival tools were better than weapons in medal conversion.
"Is it because the drone’s range or something? Why did it give so much?" Kai muttered.
However, it wasn’t actually the best!

As it turned out, the Water Gift Pack came to 7.50 Points. The gene stimulant injector was the highest at 2.40 Points, with the atmospheric water generator close behind at 2.30 Points and the Spirit-Boosting Potion for 1.7 Points.
With these three. The Water Gift Pack won the points race!
"Hahaha! Now... I’ll have the highest Survivor Medals in the upcoming Auction!"
Just like that, Kai used his Infinite Gift Pack system and summoned Water Gift Packs every few seconds to be converted with the help of the Gene Trader’s Item Conversation Tab!
Kai wasn’t even done when the sky had already begun to darken.

The day had slipped away as he dared not stop in his conversions. Still, he had already radioed the location of the Gene Trader to the others. His message was clear... this one was selling ten Auction Tokens and that he had taken one of them.

As for the others, Vera’s team had been just as fortunate. They stumbled upon another Gene Trader in a ruined district and managed to buy out all the Auction Tokens there. The price was steep... five thousand experience points each, and a few of them leveled down after paying the cost.
The setback was quite bitter, but the tokens were too valuable to ignore.
Still, Kai’s mission was complete after a few more hours and soon, he left the Gene Trader behind and made his way back to the shelter...
This time, however, his focus had shifted. The Auction was coming, but before that, he had another plan.
It was time to use his Neural Gear and enter the mysterious Virtual World!

chapters.title: Chapter 281: New Beginner Town
paragraphs: After the matters with the Gene Trader, the Auction Token, and Survivor Medals were dealt with, Kai returned to the Blue Grass Shelter’s thatched house.
A family could live here, so it had enough space.
Then, he ordered Atom to guard him and not let anyone come close.
After giving this order, Kai opened his Inventory and took out the Neural Gear.
The device looked deceptively simple... It was a glossy, portable headset with a thin band that wrapped around the skull and a cluster of micro‐nodes designed to press against the temples and spine.
Unlike the bulky VR Pods he had used before in the Aries Faction’s VR Hall, this was compact, lightweight, and built with incredibly advanced technology.
Its surface was matte black, with faint silver lines that light up softly when powered.
[ Neural Gear ]
[ Grade: Superior Portable Device ]
[ Description: A neural synchronization unit designed for direct connection to immersive applications. Portable and self‐sustaining, it can operate continuously for 24 hours without external power.
Recharging requires connection to a standard energy source or at least a B-Grade Energy Core.
Provides adaptive comfort and full sensory immersion. Compatible with installed applications. ]
[ Note: Connection is untraceable and immune to hacking attempts. ]
[ Battery Charge: 100% ]
Kai studied the description carefully and smiled. This was supposedly a 200 Reputation Points item, but thanks to his Voucher, he was able to purchase it for half of its price.
He had already installedPerfect World, the VR game that had intrigued him since he heard it the first time.
’I wonder if there will be some quality change after using this...’Kai mused.
This time, he wouldn’t be entering through the VR Pod.
The Neural Gear would be his gateway, so he was quite curious.
He then placed the device over his head. The nodes pressed gently against his skin, adjusting automatically to fit.
Soon, a faint hum resonated through his body as the system activated.
[ Neural synchronization initializing... ]
[ Scanning vitals... ]
[ Spirit resonance detected. ]
[ Gene Skill compatibility confirmed. ]
[ Adaptive comfort engaged. ]
A tingling sensation spread across his body, as though every nerve was being mapped.
Kai clenched his fists, forcing himself to stay calm as the sensation deepened.
His vision blurred before it was filled with cascading streams of light.
[ Avatar Creation Mode ]
[ Note: Appearance locked to genetic scan for skill synchronization. Customization limited to name selection. ]
Kai blinked. "Wait... avatar creation?"
He hadn’t expected this. He had already enteredPerfect Worldbefore through the VR Pod, and his character had been synchronized directly with his genetic scan.
But this Neural Gear was different. It demanded a new identity.
This was completely different from what Cornelio had mentioned before.
[ Character Creation ]
Enter Avatar Name:
It was the same message...
’Whatever... Let’s just go with the flow.’
He didn’t want to use his real name. This was a new world, and a new identity should follow. He thought for a moment, then slowly typed...
"Traceless."
[ Name confirmed: Traceless. ]
[ Avatar creation complete. ]
Kai exhaled as he saw the acceptance...
Well, the Neural Gear had forced him to start fresh, but perhaps that was an opportunity.

Soon, the same cinematic scene appeared, showing this world being invaded by Alien races. They corrupted the land, mutated the animals into beasts, and it displayed how humanity gathered its survivors, forging factions, and built weapons to fight back.
Still, this was a game world with twelve floors, or perhaps, realms in total...
After the game introduction, he soon entered the beginning town... Which was different from the default spawn point!
[ Spawn point: Beginner Town - Reverie Town ]
The Beginner Town, when he used the VR pod, was the town of Lyra... This time, however, was completely different!
The salty breeze hit Kai the moment his vision cleared.
He blinked a few times, adjusting to the sudden brightness of the new environment.
Whoosh~ Whoosh~
He soon heard the rhythmic crash of waves against the pier.
He was standing on cobblestone streets that sloped gently toward the harbor, where dockworkers shouted orders and crates were being loaded onto a massive ship.
"A port town?" Kai muttered as he heard the faint creak of wooden planks across the port. Reverie Town seemed to be special.
He saw sailors tightening ropes, merchants haggling over goods, and adventurers preparing for voyages.
It was nothing like Lyra, the inland beginner town he had spawned in before.
Kai’s lips curved into a faint smile. "Interesting. This is new."
He took a moment to observe the details.
The town itself was quite nice. It had taverns, market stalls, and a central square visible in the distance.
Curious, Kai opened his status window.
[ Character Status ]
Name: Traceless
Titles: None
Level: 1
Health: 100 / 100
Energy: 50 / 50
Physique Rating: F+
Strength: 10
Intelligence: 10
Dexterity: 10
Endurance: 10
Vitality: 10
Reputation: 0
Faction: None
Kai nodded. "Same as before... Level 1, base stats. At least that’s consistent."
He then checked his inventory next.
[ Inventory ]
[ Slot 1: Newbie Gift Pack ]
[ Slot 2-10: Empty ]
[ Newbie Gift Pack ] Contains: Basic rations, beginner weapon voucher, 5 healing salves, 1 stamina potion.
"Standard starter kit," Kai muttered. Nothing unusual there.
But when he opened the skills list, his eyes widened.
[ Active Skills: Spirit Pulse Lv5, Specter Step Lv5, Fast Appraisal Lv5, Beast Arm Lv5 ]
[ Passive Skills: Keen Sense Lv5, Bio Adaptive Constitution Lv5, Battle Trance Lv5, Bronze Skin Lv5 ]
Kai froze. "What...? Level 5?"
He was shocked, in the VR Pod, his gene skills had reset to Level 0 inside the game. That had been the rule... Synchronization acknowledged his real abilities but forced progression from scratch.
Yet here, with the Neural Gear, his skills carried over exactly as they were in the real world.
"This... changes everything."
Then, as Kai was just about to explore the marketplace, a sudden alarm rang out across Reverie Town.
Wooo~ Wooo~
The piercing sound echoed from the central square, followed by frantic shouts.
"We’re under attack!" someone yelled.
Kai’s eyes widened. "Seriously? A beginner town being attacked?"
Then, a huge shadow blocked the sky, and soon, he realized what was attacking them!
’The heck? An alien ship this early?!’

Customization limited to name selection. ]
Kai blinked.
"Wait... avatar creation?"
He hadn’t expected this.
He had already enteredPerfect Worldbefore through the VR Pod, and his character had been synchronized directly with his genetic scan.
But this Neural Gear was different.
It demanded a new identity.
This was completely different from what Cornelio had mentioned before.
[ Character Creation ]
Enter Avatar Name:
It was the same message...
’Whatever...
Let’s just go with the flow.’
He didn’t want to use his real name.
This was a new world, and a new identity should follow.
He thought for a moment, then slowly typed...
"Traceless."
[ Name confirmed: Traceless. ]
[ Avatar creation complete. ]
Kai exhaled as he saw the acceptance...
Well, the Neural Gear had forced him to start fresh, but perhaps that was an opportunity.
Soon, the same cinematic scene appeared, showing this world being invaded by Alien races.
They corrupted the land, mutated the animals into beasts, and it displayed how humanity gathered its survivors, forging factions, and built weapons to fight back.
Still, this was a game world with twelve floors, or perhaps, realms in total...
After the game introduction, he soon entered the beginning town...
Which was different from the default spawn point!
[ Spawn point: Beginner Town - Reverie Town ]
The Beginner Town, when he used the VR pod, was the town of Lyra...
This time, however, was completely different!
The salty breeze hit Kai the moment his vision cleared.
He blinked a few times, adjusting to the sudden brightness of the new environment.
Whoosh~ Whoosh~
He soon heard the rhythmic crash of waves against the pier.
He was standing on cobblestone streets that sloped gently toward the harbor, where dockworkers shouted orders and crates were being loaded onto a massive ship.
"A port town?" Kai muttered as he heard the faint creak of wooden planks across the port.
Reverie Town seemed to be special.
He saw sailors tightening ropes, merchants haggling over goods, and adventurers preparing for voyages.
It was nothing like Lyra, the inland beginner town he had spawned in before.
Kai’s lips curved into a faint smile.
"Interesting.
This is new."
He took a moment to observe the details.
The town itself was quite nice.
It had taverns, market stalls, and a central square visible in the distance.
Curious, Kai opened his status window.
[ Character Status ]
Name: Traceless
Titles: None
Level: 1
Health: 100 / 100
Energy: 50 / 50
Physique Rating: F+
Strength: 10
Intelligence: 10
Dexterity: 10
Endurance: 10
Vitality: 10
Reputation: 0
Faction: None
Kai nodded.
"Same as before...
Level 1, base stats.
At least that’s consistent."
He then checked his inventory next.
[ Inventory ]
[ Slot 1: Newbie Gift Pack ]
[ Slot 2-10: Empty ]
[ Newbie Gift Pack ] Contains: Basic rations, beginner weapon voucher, 5 healing salves, 1 stamina potion.
"Standard starter kit," Kai muttered.
Nothing unusual there.
But when he opened the skills list, his eyes widened.
[ Active Skills: Spirit Pulse Lv5, Specter Step Lv5, Fast Appraisal Lv5, Beast Arm Lv5 ]
[ Passive Skills: Keen Sense Lv5, Bio Adaptive Constitution Lv5, Battle Trance Lv5, Bronze Skin Lv5 ]
Kai froze.
"What...?
Level 5?"
He was shocked, in the VR Pod, his gene skills had reset to Level 0 inside the game.
That had been the rule...
Synchronization acknowledged his real abilities but forced progression from scratch.
Yet here, with the Neural Gear, his skills carried over exactly as they were in the real world.
"This... changes everything."
Then, as Kai was just about to explore the marketplace, a sudden alarm rang out across Reverie Town.
Wooo~ Wooo~
The piercing sound echoed from the central square, followed by frantic shouts.
"We’re under attack!" someone yelled.
Kai’s eyes widened.
"Seriously?
A beginner town being attacked?"
Then, a huge shadow blocked the sky, and soon, he realized what was attacking them!
’The heck?
An alien ship this early?!’

chapters.title: Chapter 282: The New Skill
paragraphs: Kai barely had the time to react when he saw the sky split open as beams of light rained down from the alien vessel!
He immediately tried to hide since he knew that dying here meant that he wouldn’t be able to log back in for the next 24 hours!
Thankfully, as the bombardment shook Reverie Town’s foundations, splintering rooftops and sending shockwaves across the harbor, the defenders immediately acted...
A mage from the manor raised his staff, conjuring a massive barrier that glowed like glass, absorbing the next volley.
After that, warriors leapt forward as they intercepted the descending beams, cutting through the energy with their own skills!
One figure even soared into the sky. This person had wings of light from his back as he blocked the bombardment head‐on...
Bang! Bang! Bang!
The first assault was repelled, but the alien ship hovered ominously above, its cannons charging again.
Kai, or rather, Traceless, watched in awe.
"I guess this isn’t a normal beginner town, huh..."
Soon, the alien vessel unleashed another barrage, but this time humanity answered in kind. From the horizon, fast flying crafts emerged, their hulls gleaming with faction insignias.
Just like that, the residents celebrated!
As it turned out, it was their town’s aerial force!
They were called Skybreaker Frigates, Dawnwing Cruisers, Ironclad Gunships...
The ships moved into formation, unleashing volleys of plasma and artillery fire against the alien vessel. The sky became a battlefield with beams and explosions colliding in midair.
Kai’s heart raced. He had seen the cinematic introduction, but witnessing it firsthand was different. This battle was quite chaotic and terrifying.
Soon, the Alien Ship backed off...
Then came the monsters.
"Monsters! Block them!"
"Protect the wall!"
As the alien ship bombarded the town, it actually released a strange powder that drifted across the streets and fields. The substance shimmered faintly, and Kai overheard frantic shouts...
"They’re calling the beasts!"
"I knew it... Those powders are too suspicious."
The powder acted like a beacon, summoning every monster in the surrounding region.
From the forests and hills, mutated creatures emerged... wolves with horns and long fangs, scaled boars, and insectoid horrors that were rushing towards their town.
The alien ship had basically completed its mission, and just like that, it also withdrew into the clouds.
However, the human vessels pursued, vanishing into the distance. But the monsters remained, converging on Reverie Town!
"Protect the town!"
"They’re just higher in number! They’re weak!"
The defenders rallied at the walls. Adventurers scrambled to form parties, while guards barked orders.
Kai, still Level 1, was swept up in the chaos.
"You! Newbie!" a guard shouted, tossing him a sling. "Get to the wall! Throw rocks, anything! We need every hand!"
Kai blinked, then gripped the crude weapon. He climbed the battlements, joining dozens of other beginners armed with slings, bows, and improvised weapons.
Kai then found an opportunity to open his Newbie Gift Packs...
Soon, he got basic rations, a beginner weapon voucher, 5 healing salves, and 1 stamina potion... The reason he opened this while being attacked was to actually use his Weapon Voucher to get a spear!
Below, the monsters clawed at the gates. Kai hurled a stone, striking a beast’s shoulder. It wasn’t enough to kill, but an arrow pierced its head, and the system responded.
He had participated in the subjugation, and he was getting experience points despite not getting the last hit!
His eyes widened. "R-right... Even without the last hit... I still get points?"
Excitement surged through him. He hurled another stone, then another, each strike adding to his tally.
The defenders’ coordinated attacks shredded the monsters, and Kai’s steady contributions kept the notifications coming.
The battle raged for nearly an hour.
Kai’s arms ached, but he refused to stop. Every stone mattered, every strike counted his experience points...
Soon, the monsters fell one by one, until the last of them collapsed beneath the defenders’ blades.
Then, the system chimed.
[ Level Up! ]
[ Level Up! ]
[ You have reached Level 5. ]
Kai stared at the glowing notifications, stunned. "Already... Level 5?"
He laughed, exhilarated. "Wow... this is actually nice."
From the walls, he looked out at the battlefield.
The corpses of beasts littered the ground, and the defenders cheered their victory.
Reverie Town had survived the assault, and Kai, a supposed beginner, had benefited a lot from it
As the cheers echoed across Reverie Town, Kai couldn’t help but feel curious about the monsters below...
He wanted to check them out...
However, he noticed someone approaching.
From the stairway, a figure came closer. It was the leader of the guards.
His armor was dented from battle, but his eyes were filled with energy as he scanned the recruits who had fought on the wall.
When they landed on Kai, he gave a satisfied nod.
"You fought well, newbie," the guard leader said.
"I was watching. You didn’t hesitate to help us at all... even when the monsters pressed hardest."
Kai straightened as he didn’t expect to be appreciated like that...
"I... just did what I could."
The leader’s lips curved into a faint smile. "That’s enough. Name?"
Kai hesitated, then replied firmly, "Traceless."
The guard leader reached into his belt pouch and withdrew a rolled parchment.
With a flick of his wrist, he handed it to Kai.
"Then take this. You’ve earned it."
Kai unrolled the scroll, and the system immediately responded.
[ Skill Scroll Activated ]
[ New Skill Acquired: Armored Dash ]
[ Description: A guard skill that allows the user to surge forward with reinforced defense, reducing incoming damage while closing distance to the enemy.
Cost: 7 Energy Points per Activation ]
Kai’s eyes widened as the notification appeared.
His Active Skills list updated instantly, Armored Dash joining Spirit Pulse, Specter Step, and the others.
He clenched his fists, feeling the new energy ripple through his body.
’A guard skill... given to me directly?’
Then, curiosity gnawed at him. If he could gain skills here, would they carry back into reality? As if the system had heard his thoughts, another notification appeared.
[ Synchronization Notice: Skills acquired in Perfect World will be retained upon logout. ]
Kai froze, stunned. "So... I can take this back?"
The realization sent a thrill through him.
Perfect World wasn’t just a game... it was a gateway to real power.

chapters.title: Chapter 284: The Merchants
paragraphs: The arrival of the merchant caravan sent waves of excitement through Blue Grass Shelter. Survivors gathered quickly... These thirty or so people had never seen anything like this before.

The three wagons rolled into the settlement, each guarded by a dozen heavily armed men. The guards weren’t ordinary fighters... they carried a strange device strapped to their belts, a box with antennae that pulsed faintly with blue light.
Vera and the others exchanged glances.
"Signal jammers," someone muttered. "That must be how they avoid detection from the A.I. Army."

In this apocalyptic world, where flying drones, Sentinels, and other A.I. Units scoured the land for survivors, such a device was priceless. The caravan’s safe arrival meant these merchants had mastered survival in ways few others had.
Two men stepped forward from the lead wagon.
One was tall, broad‐shouldered, with a trimmed beard and squinted eyes. The other was leaner, with a quick smile and a clear voice that could be heard by everyone.
"I am Diego," the first announced with a low voice. "And I am Santiago," the second added, bowing slightly.

Together, they spread their arms as if unveiling a treasure. "We are merchants of fortune, wanderers of the wasteland. We bring goods that many would envy, products gathered from ruins, caches, and forgotten vaults. Today, your shelter will see what others only dream of."
The crowd murmured with anticipation as Vera stepped forward...
Since Atom was watching and they were also well-equipped, they weren’t really scared of these newcomers.
"Show us what you’ve brought." Vera replied.
Diego gestured to the first wagon. The guards pulled back the canvas cover, revealing racks of weapons neatly arranged.

"This," Diego said proudly, "is our armory. Swords, spears, crossbows, and even a few firearms salvaged from military depots. Each has been cleaned, repaired, and tested. We know survivors need strength, and strength begins with steel."
To be honest, none of them really liked swords or spears. After all, they were up against machines. Swords weren’t something they’d normally wish to have when fighting against them.
Blunt weapons, explosives, tasers, or perhaps anything that could fry up the circuits of the machines would be a great option.
Well, unless you were Kai, Farrah, Alfie, Claire, and others who could brute force the A.I. soldiers, swords and spears weren’t really the best out there.
Still, the crowd looked quite excited at the sight of the sturdy bows...

The bolts were thick and seemed like they would pack a punch against the machines. Some of the firearms were rare... They were compact rifles with limited ammunition, but still deadly against mutants and other weaker A.I. units.
Santiago moved to the second wagon, pulling back its cover with a flourish. "And here, the comforts of life. Food, fruits, and supplies that remind us of what the old world once had."
Inside were crates of dried meat, sacks of rice, baskets of apples and oranges, and jars of preserved vegetables.
But it wasn’t just food...

Miscellaneous items filled the shelves... They found items like candles, portable electric fans powered by small energy cells, digital cameras, shoes, hair clips, stacks of paper, and even trinkets like watches and necklaces.
"Whoa..."
"Those shoes... Do you have size 10?"
"Wait... Electric Fan? How many do you have?"
"I want to trade my five C-Grade Energy Cores for a digital camera, that laptop, that stack of paper and that printer..."

Diego heard this and shook his head at the man. "No... For that, it’s actually worth 15 C-Grade Energy Cores. Trust me, it will be hard for you to find these things outside. They’re expensive because they’re rare, even if they’re simple items."

Santiago then cleared his throat before he continued for Diego, "Well, life is more than battle. Instead of just training and hunting, these food and devices we brought might give you warmth, memory, and entertainment. Just like what my friend said, these items may seem simple, but they restore hope..."
Vera’s group exchanged glances. The second wagon was a treasure trove of everyday necessities, things they hadn’t seen in months.
Still, they weren’t sure if they would want to actually spend a lot of Energy Cores for that.
Then Diego and Santiago approached the third wagon. Their voices lowered, becoming almost reverent.
"And here," Diego said, "is what sets us apart."
The guards carefully uncovered the last wagon. Inside were rows of locked crates, each of them were being protected by special materials.
Santiago’s grin widened.

"Gene Enhancements," he declared. "Not just the Alpha, Emerald, or Crimson Serums you’ve heard of. We stumbled upon a secret stash, a vault untouched by the A.I. Army. And within it... were these treasures."
Gasps rippled through the crowd.

They weren’t sure if these guys were just trying to make them rare and sell for a high price but if they were indeed better Gene Enhancement Serum from the Gene Traders, they wouldn’t really mind spending a bit more money.
After all, there was a limit to the Gene Enhancement Serums that they could consume.
For example, most of them now had to wait for thirty days before they could consider taking more Alpha Gene Enhancements. It was a safe serum, but the chance of getting Gene Skill was simply too low.
They had obtained high Vitality, Strength, and Spirit Energy from such a serum but it wasn’t enough anymore.
"Does it have better effects than Prime Gene, Super Gene, and others?"

Diego just smiled and nodded. "Of course! But you can say that they have a different way of helping your Genes improve. Ahem... This is our Nova Gene Enhancement Serum... I can guarantee you that if you had at least 5 of these within your body, you’d get an explosive Gene Skill for sure! If you did not get a Gene Skill, we will be paying you back!"
Diege said confidence.
"What?"
"Guaranteed?"
"Now now... I have dibs on that then."
"Don’t worry... We have plenty of them, you will be able to have yours."
"Wait... I thought they were rare? Can you actually produce these Serums?"
"Ahh... No. It’s not like that. We just found quite a lot of them in the process. We don’t make these things."
Well, no one could really confirm this matter.
Still, the fact that they have a money-back guarantee made him sound a bit more trustworthy.
He then changed the topic as he lifted one of the crates, opening it to reveal a cube the size of a fist. It pulsed faintly, dormant but alive.

"These cubes..." he said, "are Gene Weapons. But not the usual kind. These are defensive Gene Weapons, identified and appraised by experts. As you can see, they were all in their dormant cube form, waiting to be awakened. Once bound to their owner, they manifest as shields, armor, or protective gear. Do not expect swords, spears, or guns. These are defensive items..."
The crowd murmured again in disbelief.
Defensive Gene Weapons were rare, and while they lacked offensive power, their value was undeniable.
In a world where survival often hinged on endurance, armor and shields could mean the difference between life and death.
Santiago raised his hands dramatically.

"We have twenty of these cubes! Twenty! Enough to change the fate of a guild, a faction, or a shelter. Imagine your defenders clad in Gene Armor, your scouts protected by Gene Shields. Facing the Sentinels would no longer be impossible!
Vera’s eyes widened. She had her own Gene Weapon after the previous Global Events... but never defensive ones.
She turned to her companions, whispering, "This... this could make Blue Grass Shelter untouchable. We have to get them all. Atom wouldn’t be here forever."
Steven and Juno nodded as they also wanted such an item.
Diego and Santiago exchanged satisfied glances. They knew the impact of their words.
Survivors were desperate for any edge, and defensive Gene Weapons were a rare edge indeed.

"Of course," Diego added, his tone practical, "such items are not cheap. Survivor Medals will be required. But think of what you gain. Protection... Security... and the ability to withstand assaults that would crush lesser shelters."
The guards were clearly impressed and knew that they had to get one.
Seeing their reaction, the merchants’ confidence was unshakable.
Santiago leaned closer to Vera as he believed that she was the leader of this shelter...

"You must have a lot of Survivor Medals... Do you want me to give you suggestions? You should have enough to claim one or two of these treasures... If you want, I can test your affinity and give you better options."
Vera’s heart raced.

The Auction Event was already a golden opportunity to use her Survivor Medals... but this... this was immediate power. She glanced at the wagons again, at the weapons, the food, and finally the Gene Weapons.
"Wait... How long will you be staying here, Sir Merchants?"
Diego’s eyes shifted as if he was recalling their schedule before he answered.
"We’ll only stay here for six hours, Miss..." As he said this, his eyes soon noticed a familiar Sentinel Unit dressed like a normal person.
"Huh? Isn’t that Atom?"
